item.title: ‘This combo feels so illegal’: Cricket fans react as Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blitz NZ in 199-run chase
item.description: ‘This combo feels so illegal’: Cricket fans react as Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blitz NZ in 199-run chase originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi put on a world-record 118 in the powerplay at Wellington. India chased 199 in 13.2 overs to take the series 3-0 with two matches to play. Irfan Pathan and Vikrant Gupta were among those reacting to the opening stand. Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi tear New Zealand apart in Wellington India were 118 without loss after six overs chasing 199 at the Hnry Stadium on Tuesday, which is the highest powerplay score in the history of men's T20Is. New Zealand had posted 198 for 3 with Daryl Mitchell unbeaten on 89, and the match was effectively finished before their bowlers had worked out what was happening. Abhishek Sharma did most of the damage, reaching fifty off 15 balls and his hundred off 35, equalling Rohit Sharma's mark as the fastest by an Indian in the format. He finished with 113 from 38 deliveries at a strike rate of 297, hitting nine fours and 11 sixes before falling to Kyle Jamieson in the 10th over. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was the junior partner in every sense, but still made 45 off 19. The pair's 118 beat Romania's 116 against Serbia in 2021 as the all-time record and went well past Australia's 113 for 1 against Scotland, which had been the best by a full member. Naman Dhir hit the winning boundary off Jamieson with 40 balls to spare, giving India a 3-0 lead in the series with two matches still to come. MORE: IND vs NZ 3rd T20I 2026: Abhishek steals the show with a blistering ton as India clinch series The cricket world reacts to India's record opening stand The reaction began while Abhishek was still batting, and most of it settled on the same thing, which was the sheer unfairness of the two left-handers opening together. "Flat pitch + small ground + Vaibhav and Abhishek opening. This combo feels so illegal lol," one fan wrote . Flat pitch + small ground + Vaibhav and Abhishek opening This combo feels so illegal lol — (@PedriMyluv) October 27, 2026 Vikrant Gupta, the Aaj Tak sports editor, could not place it against anything he had watched before. "Haven't seen this kind of batting. Abhishek and Vaibhav as a Jodi are #IndvsNZ," he wrote . Haven't seen this kind of batting. Abhishek and Vaibhav as a Jodi are #IndvsNZ — Vikrant Gupta (@vikrantgupta73) October 27, 2026 The sharpest observation came from a fan who had noticed what the pairing was doing to Abhishek himself, with the senior man taking singles off the last ball of overs to keep himself on strike. "Get Vaibhav to open, it creates such rivalry that even Abhishek wants to farm strike by taking a single on the last ball of the over, and show his six hitting prowess," they posted . Nitin K Srivastav of Sports Tak took the discussion back to the dressing room and the coach. "What a win – fantastic. Gautam Gambhir

Abhishek and Vaibhav as a Jodi are #IndvsNZ — Vikrant Gupta (@vikrantgupta73) October 27, 2026 The sharpest observation came from a fan who had noticed what the pairing was doing to Abhishek himself, with the senior man taking singles off the last ball of overs to keep himself on strike. "Get Vaibhav to open, it creates such rivalry that even Abhishek wants to farm strike by taking a single on the last ball of the over, and show his six hitting prowess," they posted . Nitin K Srivastav of Sports Tak took the discussion back to the dressing room and the coach. "What a win – fantastic. Gautam Gambhir's fearless cricketing vision is on display as India chase 199 against New Zealand," he wrote , crediting Sooryavanshi's youthful aggression and Abhishek's attacking approach as the brand of cricket India wants to play. Irfan Pathan's response was the funniest, mocking the idea that anyone could have done anything about it. "Kisi ko to rokna chahiye tha,are kon rokega?Abhishek Sharma,Vaibhav suryavanshi ke ese start ke baad (Someone should have stopped him, right? Who would stop him? After Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Suryavanshi's such a start)," the former India all-rounder said . Someone should have stopped him, right? Who would stop him? After Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Suryavanshi's such a start — Irfan Pathan (@IrfanPathan) October 27, 2026 What ran through almost all of it was the same note of disbelief rather than celebration. New Zealand had made 198 on a ground where the first-innings average is 153, which on most nights is a winning score. Nobody watching seemed quite able to process that it had been chased down in just 14 overs. But now that the series is already won, comes a complicated question. MORE: Daren Sammy sarcastically questions what makes India a 'dangerous' team in cricket Who should open in the fourth T20I at Eden Park? India go to Auckland on October 30 with the series already won and two dead rubbers to fill, which is the one situation in which a side can afford to be curious. The obvious call is to leave it alone, after Abhishek and Sooryavanshi's historic night. Though, Samson should still be the first-choice opener when Ishan Kishan returns from injury. item.title: Relief for Real Madrid as key player avoids significant injury in El Clasico win
item.description: Relief for Real Madrid as key player avoids significant injury in El Clasico win Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde has avoided any significant injury in preliminary tests after playing through muscular discomfort during his team’s 2-1 victory over Barcelona in El Clasico . According to The Athletic’s Guillermo Rai , initial examinations have revealed no major damage, although the midfielder’s condition remains subject to further assessment. Valverde experienced hamstring discomfort during the first half but continued playing well into the second before eventually being forced off. His decision to carry on despite the pain drew praise from manager Jose Mourinho after the match. Preliminary tests offer positive news for Real Madrid The initial assessment suggests that Valverde has escaped a serious injury, providing some relief for Real Madrid after the captain’s concerning display of discomfort against Barcelona. The midfielder played for approximately 40 minutes while dealing with the problem, as Mourinho disclosed after the match. Valverde was taken off during El Clasico. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) However, the preliminary findings do not rule out an injury entirely, and further evaluation will be needed to determine the extent of the issue and his availability for upcoming fixtures. Speaking to the media, Valverde addressed the concern after the final whistle, admitting that he had experienced considerable pain during the game. “I had a lot of pain in my leg, but hopefully I’m not injured. I think it was just a precaution. The coach asked me if I could play despite the pain, and of course I said yes,” the Real Madrid captain explained . “The most important thing is to help the team win,” he added. Mourinho praises Valverde for playing through pain Mourinho was keen to acknowledge Valverde’s contribution after Real Madrid secured an important victory over their rivals. Valverde has avoided a significant injury. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) The manager highlighted the captain’s determination to remain on the pitch despite his physical discomfort. “There is another name I didn’t want to leave unmentioned, and that is Valverde, for playing injured for more than 40 minutes,” Mourinho said after the match. “He got injured, wanted to carry on and push himself to his limits, and gave everything while he was on the pitch,” the Portuguese coach added. Valverde’s willingness to continue reflected his commitment to the team and there will be relief that the club captain has avoided a significant injury. Their next steps will depend on the results of further examinations.

item.title: 2 Red Wings Named Top Trade Targets
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have spent months navigating the uncertain futures of Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson , but the latest NHL trade rankings provide another troubling reminder of just how complicated things have become in Hockeytown. Two players who were supposed to be major pieces of Detroit’s future now occupy the top two spots on one prominent insider’s trade board. Chris Johnston of The Athletic has ranked Larkin No. 1 and Edvinsson No. 2 on his latest NHL Trade Board, putting the Red Wings in the uncomfortable position of having the league’s two highest-ranked trade candidates on the same roster. For interim general manager Shawn Horcoff, the situation presents two very different challenges that could have enormous implications for the franchise moving forward. Oct 24, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin (71) skates with the puck against the Calgary Flames during the second period at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dylan Larkin Ranked No. 1 on NHL Trade Board Larkin landing at No. 1 should not come as a complete surprise, considering his desire to leave Detroit has been public knowledge since the offseason. The 30-year-old center requested a trade following the 2025-26 campaign, and despite returning to the Red Wings this season, there has been no indication that his position has changed. Johnston’s latest trade board highlights Larkin’s skating ability and five consecutive 30-goal seasons as major reasons he remains such an attractive potential addition for other organizations. His $8.7 million annual salary-cap hit through the 2030-31 season also means an acquiring team would be making a significant long-term commitment rather than simply renting a player for a playoff run. Perhaps the most interesting development involves Larkin’s willingness to expand his list of acceptable trade destinations. The former Red Wings captain has indicated he would approve a move to 10 teams, although the Montreal Canadiens and Buffalo Sabres reportedly have interest despite not being included on that list. That creates an obvious obstacle for Detroit, because interest from another organization means little if Larkin isn’t willing to approve the destination. Johnston suggests that the list could eventually need to grow further if the Red Wings are going to find a package that satisfies both the player and the organization. The latest ranking comes shortly after the Red Wings were reportedly presented with multiple trade offers for Larkin , with Horcoff continuing to hold out for a stronger return. Detroit appears determined not to move its longtime center simply for the sake of resolving an uncomfortable situation. Johnston’s assessment points toward Larkin eventually being traded during the 2026-27 season, though no agreement has been announced. item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings have spent months navigating the uncertain futures of Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson , but the latest NHL trade rankings provide another troubling reminder of just how complicated things have become in Hockeytown. Two players who were supposed to be major pieces of Detroit’s future now occupy the top two spots on one prominent insider’s trade board. Chris Johnston of The Athletic has ranked Larkin No. 1 and Edvinsson No. 2 on his latest NHL Trade Board, putting the Red Wings in the uncomfortable position of having the league’s two highest-ranked trade candidates on the same roster. For interim general manager Shawn Horcoff, the situation presents two very different challenges that could have enormous implications for the franchise moving forward. Oct 24, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin (71) skates with the puck against the Calgary Flames during the second period at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dylan Larkin Ranked No. 1 on NHL Trade Board Larkin landing at No. 1 should not come as a complete surprise, considering his desire to leave Detroit has been public knowledge since the offseason. The 30-year-old center requested a trade following the 2025-26 campaign, and despite returning to the Red Wings this season, there has been no indication that his position has changed. Johnston’s latest trade board highlights Larkin’s skating ability and five consecutive 30-goal seasons as major reasons he remains such an attractive potential addition for other organizations. His $8.7 million annual salary-cap hit through the 2030-31 season also means an acquiring team would be making a significant long-term commitment rather than simply renting a player for a playoff run. Perhaps the most interesting development involves Larkin’s willingness to expand his list of acceptable trade destinations. The former Red Wings captain has indicated he would approve a move to 10 teams, although the Montreal Canadiens and Buffalo Sabres reportedly have interest despite not being included on that list. That creates an obvious obstacle for Detroit, because interest from another organization means little if Larkin isn’t willing to approve the destination. Johnston suggests that the list could eventually need to grow further if the Red Wings are going to find a package that satisfies both the player and the organization. The latest ranking comes shortly after the Red Wings were reportedly presented with multiple trade offers for Larkin , with Horcoff continuing to hold out for a stronger return. Detroit appears determined not to move its longtime center simply for the sake of resolving an uncomfortable situation. Johnston’s assessment points toward Larkin eventually being traded during the 2026-27 season, though no agreement has been announced. Until an acceptable offer arrives and Larkin approves the destination, his future will remain one of the NHL’s most closely watched situations. Simon Edvinsson Ranked No. 2 as Contract Standoff Continues While Larkin’s place atop the trade board was somewhat predictable, Edvinsson occupying the second spot may be even more concerning for Red Wings fans. The 23-year-old defenseman was supposed to be a cornerstone of Detroit’s blue line for years, but his unresolved contract situation has left the organization facing another potentially significant departure. Edvinsson remains unsigned as a restricted free agent after averaging approximately 22 minutes of ice time per game last season. He attended training camp in September without a contract, and negotiations have yet to produce an agreement that would allow him to return to Detroit’s lineup. Johnston reports that Edvinsson would prefer a fresh start elsewhere, although his situation is different from Larkin’s because he has not submitted a formal trade request. The young defenseman reportedly believes moving on may be the best outcome following a lengthy and unsuccessful contract negotiation. The biggest concern for Detroit is the approaching December 1 signing deadline , which Edvinsson must meet to remain eligible to play in the NHL this season. Every passing week without an agreement increases the possibility that the Red Wings could lose an entire season of development from one of their most important young players. Horcoff, however, has made his position clear regarding the organization’s desire to keep Edvinsson. On October 14, the interim general manager said he had no interest in trading the defenseman , emphasizing that Detroit remains focused on reaching a contract agreement. That stance creates a significant contrast between the organization’s plans and the direction Edvinsson reportedly wants to take. Detroit would prefer to retain a 6-foot-6 defenseman with outstanding mobility and top-pairing potential, but convincing him to commit to the franchise may prove increasingly difficult. Red Wings Could Be Facing Two Franchise-Altering Decisions The most concerning aspect of Johnston’s rankings isn’t simply that Detroit has two players on the trade board. It’s that Larkin and Edvinsson represent two of the most difficult types of NHL talent to replace: an established offensive center and a young, potentially elite defenseman. Larkin has already demonstrated that he can produce at a high level, scoring 34 goals last season while extending his streak of 30-goal campaigns. Edvinsson, meanwhile, offers a rare combination of size, skating ability, and defensive potential that organizations typically spend years trying to acquire. Losing either player would leave a substantial hole in Detroit’s roster, but losing both could fundamentally alter the organization’s direction. Instead of building around two established pieces, the Red Wings could find themselves searching for replacements at two premium positions. That possibility may help explain why Detroit has reportedly been exploring a specific type of return in recent trade discussions. As we previously reported , the organization has shown interest in acquiring young centers and high-end prospects as it evaluates potential moves involving Larkin and Edvinsson. Elliotte Friedman has also reported that Detroit is asking about young centers , although it remains unclear whether those conversations relate primarily to Larkin, Edvinsson, or both players. That distinction is important because the organization continues to publicly express a desire to retain Edvinsson rather than trade him. Horcoff faces the difficult task of protecting Detroit’s future while managing two situations that have already become major distractions. Trading Larkin might eventually become unavoidable, but surrendering Edvinsson before exhausting every realistic possibility of signing him would represent a much different organizational decision. What’s Next for Larkin, Edvinsson and the Red Wings? Johnston ranking both players at the top of his trade board doesn’t mean the Red Wings are preparing to announce two blockbuster deals. Trade rankings reflect an insider’s assessment of the market and the likelihood of movement, not confirmation that a transaction is imminent. Larkin’s situation centers on finding the right trade partner and obtaining a return that Detroit considers acceptable. Edvinsson’s situation, on the other hand, remains tied to a contract stalemate that could become significantly more consequential as December 1 approaches. For Red Wings fans, seeing two potential cornerstone players listed as the NHL’s top trade candidates is hardly an encouraging development. Detroit has already endured years of frustration while trying to return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs, and losing both players would introduce even more uncertainty into that process. item.title: Napoli Tipped to Get Busy and Go Young in January
item.description: Napoli Tipped to Get Busy and Go Young in January After a subdued summer, Napoli are gearing up for a more eventful January window and have earmarked several youngsters to address their needs. They are following multiple midfielders, as they aren’t very deep and have a few question marks there. According to Tuttomercatoweb , the Azzurri have joined Inter and Juventus in the race for Alessandro Romano , but it’ll be difficult to convince Cagliari to sell him during the winter. They are also after Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall, who’s not been a regular under Roberto De Zerbi, and Tomas Aranda. The Boca Juniors starlet can man multiple roles and has tallied one goal and three assists in 32 first-team outings. Moreover, they are keen on Darryl Bakola , like the Bianconeri and Roma. However, his price tag is growing very rapidly. Napoli will also need to sort out a few exits. Lorenzo Lucca’s departure would intensify their efforts to acquire Gustavo Varela from Monza. Noa Lang has had decent performances filling in for Alisson Santos. However, management will evaluate possible offers from Ajax and PSV. The same goes for David Neres, who’s been injury-prone. If the Azzurri sold a winger, they’d go for Mohamed Ali Zoma, who was recently called up by Roberto Mancini. They have also been offered Cruzeiro’s young goalie Otavio. Our Take on Napoli Their list of priorities and potential targets would be long if they determined that the squad needed to be fortified to qualify for the UCL. It was a gross miscalculation if they thought they could stroll to a top-four finish. The order has to come from above, though, as Aurelio De Laurentiis clearly tightened the purse strings last summer.

item.title: Jalen Brunson names who was to blame for NBA Finals Game 3 loss that Donald Trump attended
item.description: Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks pulled off an incredibly unlikely NBA Finals win against the San Antonio Spurs. While the NBA Finals win was something out of a fairy tale, it is safe to say that fans were concerned after the Knicks lost Game 3 at Madison Square Garden. Among the attendees was none other than US President Donald Trump. Some fans even blamed the loss on Trump’s presence, suggesting that he was a bad luck charm for the Knicks. Jalen Brunson jokingly suggests Eli Manning, not Donald Trump, was to blame for Game 3 loss Speaking on the ManningCast broadcast of Monday Night Football, Jalen Brunson was asked by NFL legend Peyton Manning about the New York Knicks’ Game 3 loss in the NBA Finals. Manning suggested that his brother Eli being in attendance for Game 3 led to their loss, a statement Brunson didn’t agree with, but didn’t outright reject either. Peyton Manning: “Jalen, we talked about this earlier – your Knicks went on this incredible championship run last spring. Heading into the Finals, y’all won 11 in a row, then you take the first two games in San Antonio. But then you lose Game 3 at home, that was the only game that Eli went to, and the only game you lost in the Finals. How much do you blame Eli for costing you guys the sweep?” Jalen Brunson: “I didn’t blame him then, so I’m not going to blame him now. But he hasn’t been back since, so I would love for him to pop his head back in at some point.” The loss in Game 3 came amid great fanfare about the Knicks, especially due to the massive celebrity presence at Madison Square Garden. While there were several big names at the game, perhaps no name was bigger than Donald Trump, who was invited to take in the game by Knicks owner James Dolan, who is a longtime friend of Trump’s. item.title: Mandas Tops European Charts; Leeds United & Ex-Liverpool Goalkeepers on Podium
item.description: Mandas Tops European Charts; Leeds United & Ex-Liverpool Goalkeepers on Podium Thanks to a stellar start to the season, Lazio goalkeeper Christos Mandas has the highest save percentage in Europe’s top-five Leagues. Christos Manda Has Been in Brilliant Form Last summer, the 24-year-old returned to Formello after a listless six-month loan spell at Bournemouth, where he failed to make a single appearance across all competitions. All in all, the Greek’s only outing of the 2025/26 campaign was a Coppa Italia game between Lazio and AC Milan. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Therefore, Mandas looked slightly rusty in the summer, but Gennaro Gattuso insisted he should be the club’s first choice between the sticks, sanctioning Ivan Provedel’s transfer to Inter Milan. The Calabrian head coach has been proven right, with the shot-stopper delivering superb displays in the first eight Serie A rounds of the season, playing an integral role in the seven wins registered. Mandas Outperforms All Other Serie A Goalkeepers According to La Lazio Siamo Noi , Mandas has been Italy’s best goalkeeper since the start of the season, saving 85.7% of the shots on target. His closest rival in Serie A is Napoli’s Sinisa Milinkovic-Savic (83%), followed by Roma’s Mile Svilar (81%), Cagliari’s Elija Caprile (78%), and Roma’s backup goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini (77%). Mandas Leads Europe’s Charts, Trafford & Karius on the Podium The Lazio custodian not only tops the Serie A charts, but also Europe’s top-five leagues. His closest rivals are Leeds United’s James Trafford, who was bought from Manchester City in the summer, and Schalke’s Loris Karius, mostly remembered for his nightmarish outing for Liverpool in the 2018 Champions League final against Real Madrid. They both have a save percentage of 83.3%. Sassuolo vs Lazio | Where to Watch, Insights, Lineups & Prediction While Mandas has been formidable between the sticks, Gattuso would argue that Lazio must do better at preventing chances. Nevertheless, this aspect has significantly improved in recent weeks, even though the team still conceded a late goal against Parma , albeit from a fortunate cross.

item.title: Mbappé loses brand deals in China over Mao meme remarks
item.description: French soccer player Kylian Mbappe’s image appears on the label of a sports drink produced by a Chinese manufacturer. (is associated with: «Mbappé loses brand deals in China over Mao meme remarks») Johannes Neudecker/dpa Two beverage companies in China are ending their partnerships with French football star Kylian Mbappé effective immediately. In their respective statements, both companies said they would not tolerate behaviour that offends the feelings of the Chinese people. However, the companies did not provide any further details on how Mbappé allegedly behaved inappropriately. Chinese media outlets also didn't explain the companies' decision and merely referred to statements made by Mbappé in interviews. Remarks allegedly made by the French player during a podcast interview have been circulating online. In a video that emerged on Monday, Mbappé was asked about his favourite meme featuring himself. He then mentioned one where his face had been photoshopped on to that of "some guy - I think he's a Chinese dictator." There are, for a fact, memes featuring Mbappé's face superimposed on an image of Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong. As one of the founders of the People's Republic, Mao is held in high esteem in China. Content critical of China's political leaders is generally heavily censored in the country. In a statement on Tuesday, Mbappé apologized for his comments. "During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and now I understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," the player said. "I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry." Mbappé didn't speak about the brand deals he lost. The Real Madrid forward had advertising deals with a sports drink manufacturer based in Shenzhen, southern China, and a company from Inner Mongolia that is well known in China for its dairy products. Among other things, his face appeared on the bottle labels. A second dairy product manufacturer and the influential social media platform Xiaohongshu - the equivalent of Instagram in China - also announced they were ending their partnerships with Mbappé. Meanwhile, China’s state-run television stopped airing commercials featuring the player. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun emphasized that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people would, of course, be met with united opposition from all sectors of Chinese society. The Spanish La Liga, meanwhile, said it "deeply regrets the offence caused" by the comments and stressed that they "were made in a personal capacity and do not represent" the league. "Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions, and its people, and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week,"

item.title: Matt LaFleur Sends Subtle Message on NFL Officiating After Packers’ Controversial Loss
item.description: Matt LaFleur had plenty to say after Sunday’s game in Detroit, yet he held back. The Green Bay Packers coach arrived at Ford Field after a 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys on October 18. A late loss to the Lions changed the mood quickly. Reporters wanted clear answers about a chaotic finish, and his responses revealed more than he likely intended. Matt LaFleur avoids comment on officiating after Packers loss Detroit won 20-17 when Jake Bates kicked a field goal as time expired. The loss dropped Green Bay to 4-3, and two roughing the passer flags became the biggest talking point. The first came in the third quarter with the Lions leading 17-14. Brenton Cox Jr. was flagged after being blocked into quarterback Jared Goff on a third-and-10 incompletion. That call kept a Detroit drive alive. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur reacts after a call during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The second hit Karl Brooks with the game tied at 17. Goff completed a pass to Sam LaPorta on the play, and the Fox broadcast team said it was not a foul. Tom Brady and Micah Parsons also publicly questioned the officiating. Green Bay has now been flagged for roughing the passer eight times this season, while opponents have none. NFL insider Ari Meirov noted that coaches risk fines if they criticize officials in public. That may explain why LaFleur kept his answers short. “I don’t even want to comment on any of the penalties,” when asked about the roughing calls, the coach said. “I just, it is what it is. you got to play above it, and I thought there were some tough calls but it is what it is.” #Packers HC Matt LaFleur was asked about the roughing the penalty calls “There were some tough calls but it is what it is.” https://t.co/F7AaHhteCE — Cameron Ezeir (@camezeir) October 25, 2026 This was not the first time LaFleur has chosen his words carefully on a sensitive topic. LaFleur showed similar Caution on Josh Jacobs earlier this season Matt LaFleur showed the same discretion in September when asked about running back Josh Jacobs . Jacobs was on the Commissioner’s Exempt List while the NFL reviewed his legal case. When asked if his opinion had changed, LaFleur kept it brief. “No. I know the guy, and I know the character of the guy, so I’ve said it many times. And unfortunately, situations occur in life, and it’s just an unfortunate situation,” LaFleur explained. He declined to go further when reporters asked why the team kept Jacobs on the roster if he is found guilty. “Yeah, I’m not, guys, I’m not going to get into any of this until the league completes their investigation,” LaFleur added. The NFL removed Jacobs from the list on October 19, and he returned to practice before Green Bay activated him five days later. The Packers’ running game needed him. item.title: Why did it say the word 'GOLF' on a famous soccer team's jerseys?
item.description: The Barcelona soccer team, one of the world's most renowned clubs, had a new look for its El Clásico match against Real Madrid on Sunday, Oct. 25. The La Liga champion featured its traditional blue and red kit, but its sponsor will be replaced by one word: "GOLF." Barcelona wasn't advertising that sport with clubs and a tiny white ball, but instead will be showcasing the logo of rap superstar Tyler, The Creator. In 2011, Tyler founded GOLF WANG, a streetwear and fashion brand. The company is often shortened to "Golf" on its apparel. As part of its sponsorship with Spotify, Barcelona has featured kits with logos from Karol G, Ed Sheeran, Travis Scott, Rosalía, Coldplay, The Rolling Stones and Drake. But this collaboration is slightly different. For the first time, Barcelona has handed the artist complete creative control of the capsule collection. Lamine Yamal and the men's team wore it during the rivalry game on Oct. 25 at Camp Nou. The match was the first Clásico fixture broadcast on ABC , and Real Madrid won, 2-1. As with previous editions, there are 1,899 GOLF WANG jerseys available for purchase to commemorate the year Barcelona was established. The full collection includes jerseys, jackets, T-shirts, hoodies, a water bottle, pin and sticker. “Every jersey takeover we've done has pushed us somewhere new, but this one feels different," said Marc Hazan, Spotify's senior vice president of marketing and partnerships. "Tyler brings a distinct creative world to the collaboration, extending far beyond the jersey. From the campaign visuals and collection to the immersive event in Barcelona, every element is rooted in GOLF WANG’s brand world, making this one of our most exciting collaborations with FC Barcelona yet.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why did it say the word 'GOLF' on a famous soccer team's jerseys?

item.title: England out of tri-series after Sri Lanka beat Pakistan
item.description: England play Australia and South Africa in 50-over cricket later this winter [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Lahore Pakistan 110 (25.2 overs): Babar 29; Madushanka 5-34 Sri Lanka 114-2 (18.1 overs): Kaminudu 62* Sri Lanka won by eight wickets Scorecard England are out of their 50-over tri-series in Pakistan after the hosts were beaten by Sri Lanka on Tuesday in Lahore. After three defeats from three, Harry Brook's side needed Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka to have a chance of reaching Saturday's final by beating Sri Lanka on Thursday. Instead, that match will be a dead rubber after Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out and Sri Lanka raced to their target in just 18.1 overs. Though conditions will be significantly different at next year's World Cup in southern Africa, the exit is a blow to England, who had built some momentum in their one-day international cricket this year. After their dismal World Cup defence in 2023 and exiting the Champions Trophy without winning a match last year, England had won away in Sri Lanka and beaten India and Sri Lanka at home in 2026. In Pakistan, they failed to chase 303 despite being well placed at 120-1 and then suffered two extraordinary losses. On Thursday they were unable to defend 430 as Sri Lanka pulled off the second-highest chase in ODI history and three days later a last-wicket stand of 89 secured an incredible win for Pakistan. After their tournament concludes on Thursday, England travel to Australia for a tour of three ODIs and five T20s, starting on 13 November. They are also scheduled to play a warm-up against a Western Australia XI on Saturday, 7 November in Perth. For Sri Lanka, left-armer Dilshan Madushanka landed blows before Saturday's final by taking 5-34 against Pakistan. The hosts were unable to stop the regular loss of wickets with Babar Azam the highest scorer with 29. Opener Kamindu Mendis hit 62 not out from 60 balls to secure the rapid win. Australia strike twice to peg back South Africa in decider - follow live

item.title: Rachel Clark helps lead FSU lacrosse into year two
item.description: Assistant coach Rachel Clark is in her second year coaching Florida State ’s women’s lacrosse team. Outside of her coaching responsibilities, Clark plays professionally for the Boston Guard in the Women’s Lacrosse League (WLL), where she led the league in goals and points as a rookie and was named 2026 Attacker of the Year. The Seminoles went 4-12 overall and 0-10 in Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) play in their inaugural season. As the program heads into year two, Clark, who works primarily with the offense, said the staff expects a different result. “The coaching staff has talked about it nonstop about how much we believe in this group. We were blown away by the jump from last year's team to this year's team,” Clark said to the FSView. “We're excited and I think that every single person who's a part of this staff and making this program run has 100 percent belief that we are going to make a real splash in the ACC this year.” Building a culture FSU added four transfers this summer, along with a new freshman class and changes to the coaching staff. With many new faces, Clark said the team will have to come together quickly. She’s leaning on what she learned during Boston College’s 2024 championship season, when the team’s daily approach mattered as much as its talent. Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter “The year our team was the most successful, yes we were very talented, but that's not what got us the championships,” Clark said. “It's because every single day we were practicing like it was a championship game and we were playing not for ourselves but, for example, I was playing for the seniors to play another day on the field.” On offense, Clark works with a group led last season by Meg Kenny, who finished with a team-high 43 points, and Summer Harrell, who added 37. Both recorded eight multi-goal games. A record-setting career Before she was drawing up plays, Clark was one of the most prolific scorers in college lacrosse. The Devon, Pennsylvania, native was ranked the No. 9 recruit in the Class of 2021 by Inside Lacrosse and started two seasons at University of Virginia, where she was named 2022 ACC Freshman of the Year and led the team in 2023 with 63 goals and 76 points. After transferring to Boston College, Clark led the team with 101 points and 78 goals as a junior, helping them defeat Northwestern for the 2024 national championship. item.content:encoded: Assistant coach Rachel Clark is in her second year coaching Florida State ’s women’s lacrosse team. Outside of her coaching responsibilities, Clark plays professionally for the Boston Guard in the Women’s Lacrosse League (WLL), where she led the league in goals and points as a rookie and was named 2026 Attacker of the Year. The Seminoles went 4-12 overall and 0-10 in Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) play in their inaugural season. As the program heads into year two, Clark, who works primarily with the offense, said the staff expects a different result. “The coaching staff has talked about it nonstop about how much we believe in this group. We were blown away by the jump from last year's team to this year's team,” Clark said to the FSView. “We're excited and I think that every single person who's a part of this staff and making this program run has 100 percent belief that we are going to make a real splash in the ACC this year.” Building a culture FSU added four transfers this summer, along with a new freshman class and changes to the coaching staff. With many new faces, Clark said the team will have to come together quickly. She’s leaning on what she learned during Boston College’s 2024 championship season, when the team’s daily approach mattered as much as its talent. Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter “The year our team was the most successful, yes we were very talented, but that's not what got us the championships,” Clark said. “It's because every single day we were practicing like it was a championship game and we were playing not for ourselves but, for example, I was playing for the seniors to play another day on the field.” On offense, Clark works with a group led last season by Meg Kenny, who finished with a team-high 43 points, and Summer Harrell, who added 37. Both recorded eight multi-goal games. A record-setting career Before she was drawing up plays, Clark was one of the most prolific scorers in college lacrosse. The Devon, Pennsylvania, native was ranked the No. 9 recruit in the Class of 2021 by Inside Lacrosse and started two seasons at University of Virginia, where she was named 2022 ACC Freshman of the Year and led the team in 2023 with 63 goals and 76 points. After transferring to Boston College, Clark led the team with 101 points and 78 goals as a junior, helping them defeat Northwestern for the 2024 national championship. Her senior season featured a program-record 106 goals, earning her ACC Attacker of the Year honors and a spot as a Tewaaraton Award finalist. Clark broke the previous record of 102, set by Charlotte North in 2021, with an eight-goal performance against Yale University in the 2025 NCAA quarterfinals. North, a two-time Tewaaraton winner, called Clark “one of the best goal scorers we will see in this sport,” according to the Premier Lacrosse League . Clark finished her college career with 311 goals and 380 points. She has kept scoring since, leading the WLL in its inaugural season as a rookie with 18 goals, 23 points, and the league lead in total shots for the Boston Guard. A new chapter Clark finished her playing career at Boston College in May 2025, and the ’Noles named her to their first coaching staff that July. She said the decision to coach came later than most people might expect. “I honestly didn't really plan that I was going to coach, I wouldn't say up until my senior year was when I decided that I really wanted to coach at the next level,” Clark said. “I always was thinking about nursing or teaching and after I finished playing I realized I wasn't ready to get away from the game.” Before arriving in Tallahassee, Clark coached youth players through private lessons and clubs, including Dynasty Elite Lacrosse and Philly Blast . For her, the FSU job offered a familiar conference and a fresh start. “As a player I always wanted to compete at the highest level, and when I was thinking about coaching, the same thing applied,” Clark said. “I always wanted to stay in the ACC, it’s the conference I played in. I think it’s the best conference in the country. And with a brand-new ACC program in Florida I was like, ‘I have to try for this opportunity.’” Clark’s ultimate goal for the Garnet and Gold’s spring 2027 season is to play hard and win. After a winless first run through the ACC, she said she has seen what her players can do and believes they can accomplish more within the conference. “You want to make history and we have what we need to do it, so get excited,” Clark said. “I am most looking forward to our first ACC win.” Gretchen Knight is a Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com . This article originally appeared on FSU News: Rachel Clark helps lead FSU lacrosse into year two

item.title: LSU Answers Questions After A Convincing Auburn Win
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; LSU Tigers wide receiver Jackson Harris (4) runs the ball during the second quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor In today’s world of unprecedented parity and unpredictable results, no team can take wins for granted. Consequently, the LSU Tigers had points to prove on their way to the Plains to face Auburn, regardless of most Vegas books favoring LSU by 6.5 points. But a dominant 38-17 road win on Saturday helped LSU answer lingering questions surrounding the team and boost its confidence going into the bye. LSU Answers Questions Can LSU Trust Sam Leavitt? Considering Sam Leavitt ’s league-leading eight interceptions, it’s easy to understand skepticism surrounding his ability to avoid detrimental plays. Be it a bad decision or an off-target throw, Leavitt inevitably made a pass to the opposing team every game. However, he ended that streak two weeks ago against Mississippi State. Since then, Leavitt has been more productive than any other quarterback in the SEC. The Arizona St. transfer has 76% of his passes while amassing 676 yards in the past two games. Sure, his seven touchdowns during that stretch are impressive, but the more important stat here is zero interceptions. Leavitt’s physical ability to make the throws has been apparent since his Big 12 days, but we weren’t sure if he could consistently process, go through progressions, and avoid risks. His 45 attempts against Auburn with no turnovers suggest that he can take care of the ball. Multiple factors have contributed to his improvement, but the playmaking ability of Jackson Harris has increased Leavitt’s comfort level within the offense. Leavitt has gained chemistry with Harris and trusts him to make plays in critical spots. Harris went off for 178 yards against Auburn and has four touchdowns in the last two games. Now that Trey’Dez Green has returned from injury, Leavitt has two targets he can trust to make a play in single coverage. Photo Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Is LSU a Balanced Team? The path to winning each game is obviously subjective, but a more productive, timely run game would have helped LSU in both losses. The Tigers ran effectively against Ole Miss. item.content:encoded: Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; LSU Tigers wide receiver Jackson Harris (4) runs the ball during the second quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor In today’s world of unprecedented parity and unpredictable results, no team can take wins for granted. Consequently, the LSU Tigers had points to prove on their way to the Plains to face Auburn, regardless of most Vegas books favoring LSU by 6.5 points. But a dominant 38-17 road win on Saturday helped LSU answer lingering questions surrounding the team and boost its confidence going into the bye. LSU Answers Questions Can LSU Trust Sam Leavitt? Considering Sam Leavitt ’s league-leading eight interceptions, it’s easy to understand skepticism surrounding his ability to avoid detrimental plays. Be it a bad decision or an off-target throw, Leavitt inevitably made a pass to the opposing team every game. However, he ended that streak two weeks ago against Mississippi State. Since then, Leavitt has been more productive than any other quarterback in the SEC. The Arizona St. transfer has 76% of his passes while amassing 676 yards in the past two games. Sure, his seven touchdowns during that stretch are impressive, but the more important stat here is zero interceptions. Leavitt’s physical ability to make the throws has been apparent since his Big 12 days, but we weren’t sure if he could consistently process, go through progressions, and avoid risks. His 45 attempts against Auburn with no turnovers suggest that he can take care of the ball. Multiple factors have contributed to his improvement, but the playmaking ability of Jackson Harris has increased Leavitt’s comfort level within the offense. Leavitt has gained chemistry with Harris and trusts him to make plays in critical spots. Harris went off for 178 yards against Auburn and has four touchdowns in the last two games. Now that Trey’Dez Green has returned from injury, Leavitt has two targets he can trust to make a play in single coverage. Photo Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Is LSU a Balanced Team? The path to winning each game is obviously subjective, but a more productive, timely run game would have helped LSU in both losses. The Tigers ran effectively against Ole Miss. But a more run-heavy approach early in the game could’ve taken pressure off Leavitt, who ended the game with an 86.1 total quarterback ranking according to ESPN. Dilin Jones , a back who gets stronger as the game goes on, had only 16 carries against Kentucky. Jones had 21 carries for 92 yards on the Plains. Auburn had just held a Georgia team that averages 198 rushing yards per game to 113 total rushing yards, so that makes what Jones did even more impressive. LSU’s run blocking hasn’t exactly been a strength of the team this year, but the staff’s hesitance to run has held production on the ground back more than the team’s ability to execute. The Tigers’ 34 rushes against Auburn speaks to Charlie Weis, Jr.’s commitment to the run and takes a positive step in helping LSU answer another critical question that affects its potential. Furthermore, the bye week will give Leavitt’s hamstring more time to heal, allowing him to be more of a weapon as a runner. Is the LSU defense legit? This might seem like a silly question, but LSU sits with the fourth-ranked total defense in the country. But its numbers and rankings didn’t matter when Ole Miss and Kentucky marched up and down the field seemingly at will. To the Tigers’ credit, they shifted momentum in the second half of both games but couldn’t get the timely stops at the end. Let’s face it; nobody will mistake Auburn for an offensive juggernaut. But Alex Golesh’s group piled up 192 rushing yards on its way to scoring 27 points against the SEC’s best scoring defense in Georgia. LSU’s stifling defense held Auburn to 271 total yards. Byrum Brown rushed for only 21 yards after gaining 115 a week prior. Beyond the numbers, the LSU defense played with an aggressive nature that we haven’t seen in its previous road games. The hesitation with open field tackling that hurt the Tigers against Kentucky didn’t exist. Blake Baker replaced the conservative defensive calls from Oxford with attacking, pressure-producing calls against Auburn on obvious passing downs. LSU’s assertive approach resulted in seven sacks and 12 tackles for loss on the day. Such a dominant performance against a conference opponent on the road is encouraging moving forward. The Last Word It’s a challenge to get an accurate read on any FBS college football team in 2026. Each big win seems to be followed by a disappointing loss. No teams are dominant, but some are more talented than others. LSU’s talent seems to be gelling at the right time. In hindsight, the inconsistency that plagued LSU earlier in the season should’ve been expected when considering this was almost a completely new team with a new staff. Now eight games into the season, we’re learning more about the Tigers. Leaders have emerged in the receiving room. Jordan Ross has proven to be an explosive pass-rushing complement to Princewill Umanmielen. LSU appears to be rounding into form, and it couldn’t have come at a better time with Alabama, Texas, and Tennessee up next. item.title: Every player from Alabama to play for the Boston Celtics - Roy Rogers
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from Alabama who have played for Boston. Our focus in this article is Roy Rogers. An alum of Alabama, he was picked up with the 22nd overall selection of the 1996 NBA Draft by the (then) Vancouver (now, Memphis) Grizzlies. The Linden, Alabama native played the first season of his pro career with Vancouver before he was dealt to Boston in 1997. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the Toronto Raptors in 1998. During his time suiting up for the Celtics, Rogers put up 0.8 points per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Celtics Wire: Every player from Alabama to play for the Boston Celtics - Roy Rogers

item.title: Bournemouth offer to break a club record to keep Arsenal target
item.description: Bournemouth offer to break a club record to keep Arsenal target Bournemouth is keen to keep Alex Scott, with Arsenal circling the midfielder ahead of the end of this season, and they are just one of several top teams that want to sign him. The England star has been one of the best midfielders in the Premier League over the last few seasons and continues to shine each time he plays. He was one of the key men who helped them finish in a Europa League spot at the end of last season, and he could have changed clubs that summer. However, Bournemouth refused to sell and hoped he would sign a new deal, a gamble that is not paying off as he has refused to extend his deal. Arsenal’s Interest in Scott This is good news for Arsenal, who are preparing to make an approach for him as they know rivals like Liverpool are also interested in a move for the midfielder. However, Team Talk says Bournemouth’s owner has now agreed to break their wage records to keep him at the club and is doing everything possible to make the Englishman stay on the team. The midfielder’s quality is not in question, and his performances have caught the eye of the big clubs. Arsenal’s interest is genuine, but the competition is fierce, and Bournemouth’s efforts to keep him could complicate matters. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) The Battle for His Signature Scott is one of the top players in the league, and he and his representative know the time has come to join a bigger club, so there is a fine chance he will still not sign that contract . The midfielder’s ambition is clear, and a move to a bigger club could be on the cards. The Gunners’ need for a midfielder is clear, and Scott fits the profile, but the competition from Liverpool makes the task harder. The fans will be hoping the club can get the deal done, as his quality would strengthen the squad. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. However, Team Talk says Bournemouth’s owner has now agreed to break their wage records to keep him at the club and is doing everything possible to make the Englishman stay on the team. The midfielder’s quality is not in question, and his performances have caught the eye of the big clubs. Arsenal’s interest is genuine, but the competition is fierce, and Bournemouth’s efforts to keep him could complicate matters. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) The Battle for His Signature Scott is one of the top players in the league, and he and his representative know the time has come to join a bigger club, so there is a fine chance he will still not sign that contract . The midfielder’s ambition is clear, and a move to a bigger club could be on the cards. The Gunners’ need for a midfielder is clear, and Scott fits the profile, but the competition from Liverpool makes the task harder. The fans will be hoping the club can get the deal done, as his quality would strengthen the squad. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: How should Mets rebuild bullpen for 2027? Breaking down the internal and external options
item.description: When ranking the Mets ' offseason needs, finding an ace to front a promising young rotation is right at the top. Beyond that, New York still has a glaring hole at first base, which they should aim to fill with a legitimate offensive upgrade to their in-house options. But while the rotation and first base might be 1A and 1B on the Mets' checklist, rebuilding the bullpen isn't far behind. The Mets' relief corps was a strength in 2026, both before and after the trade deadline sell-off that saw four late-inning arms (two pending free agents, two players under team control beyond 2026) shipped off. Overall in 2026, New York's bullpen ERA was 3.76, which ranked 10th in MLB and was just a tick below the Dodgers (3.74 ERA). Of the nine teams who finished with a better bullpen ERA than the Mets, eight of them reached the postseason, with the Brewers (No. 3) making it all the way to the World Series. So New York clearly has something to build on. And for all of David Stearns ' missteps in 2026, he deserves credit for building a strong bullpen ahead of the season and pressing the right buttons to keep it humming even after so many key members were traded. Still, there are big questions when it comes to who will be closing games in 2027, whether Kodai Senga will be a factor in relief , and which relievers who shined down the stretch can be counted on. Who are the Mets' bullpen options for 2027, and how should they proceed? Let's break it down... The Internal Options If you had to list pitchers who are guaranteed to be in the bullpen -- assuming everyone is healthy -- on Opening Day of 2027, there would probably just be one name on the list: Devin Williams . There are other likely members, including Daniel Duarte and Austin Warren (who are both out of minor league options). Left-hander Nate Lavender , who excelled down the stretch this season in what was his first taste of the majors, also feels like close to a lock. But there are lots of questions beyond that. Senga acclimated well when he was shifted to a late-inning relief role this past season, and his fastball/forkball combination played up. But his preference is to start. item.content:encoded: When ranking the Mets ' offseason needs, finding an ace to front a promising young rotation is right at the top. Beyond that, New York still has a glaring hole at first base, which they should aim to fill with a legitimate offensive upgrade to their in-house options. But while the rotation and first base might be 1A and 1B on the Mets' checklist, rebuilding the bullpen isn't far behind. The Mets' relief corps was a strength in 2026, both before and after the trade deadline sell-off that saw four late-inning arms (two pending free agents, two players under team control beyond 2026) shipped off. Overall in 2026, New York's bullpen ERA was 3.76, which ranked 10th in MLB and was just a tick below the Dodgers (3.74 ERA). Of the nine teams who finished with a better bullpen ERA than the Mets, eight of them reached the postseason, with the Brewers (No. 3) making it all the way to the World Series. So New York clearly has something to build on. And for all of David Stearns ' missteps in 2026, he deserves credit for building a strong bullpen ahead of the season and pressing the right buttons to keep it humming even after so many key members were traded. Still, there are big questions when it comes to who will be closing games in 2027, whether Kodai Senga will be a factor in relief , and which relievers who shined down the stretch can be counted on. Who are the Mets' bullpen options for 2027, and how should they proceed? Let's break it down... The Internal Options If you had to list pitchers who are guaranteed to be in the bullpen -- assuming everyone is healthy -- on Opening Day of 2027, there would probably just be one name on the list: Devin Williams . There are other likely members, including Daniel Duarte and Austin Warren (who are both out of minor league options). Left-hander Nate Lavender , who excelled down the stretch this season in what was his first taste of the majors, also feels like close to a lock. But there are lots of questions beyond that. Kodai Senga / Getty Images/Envato Elements/SNY Treated Image A huge variable exists when it comes to Senga. Senga acclimated well when he was shifted to a late-inning relief role this past season, and his fastball/forkball combination played up. But his preference is to start. Beyond that, it is fair to wonder whether his health would hold up over a full season of short-relief usage, and whether he's suited for the role given his meticulous routines. Reed Garrett could be a key cog if he's back healthy, which is the expectation after he spent the last year-plus recovering from Tommy John surgery. But he hasn't pitched in a big league game since September of 2025. Dedniel Núñez , who emerged as a late-game arm in 2024 and missed 2025 after having TJS, rounded into form after returning last season and was very impressive -- posting a 3.32 ERA and 0.89 WHIP in 19 innings. While he figures to be a key part of the bullpen next season, he has minor league options remaining, meaning New York could possibly start him in the minors if there's a roster crunch. Lefty Cionel Perez is an interesting case, since he's arbitration-eligible and out of minor league options. During a nine-year career with the Orioles, Astros, Reds, Nationals, and Mets, Perez has shown enough to keep getting chances. He had a terrific season for Baltimore in 2022 (1.40 ERA in 57.2 innings) and was also good for the O's in 2023 (3.54 ERA in 53.1 innings), but it's been tough sledding since then. Over the last three years, Perez has a 5.30 ERA and 1.55 WHIP in 120.2 innings. However, Perez was solid for the Mets in 24 appearances over 29.1 innings in 2026, with a 3.99 ERA (3.75 FIP) and 1.33 WHIP while walking just 2.5 per nine and striking out 10.7 per nine. Perez also has a fastball that can touch close to 99 mph, so perhaps the Mets roll the dice and see if they can unlock what made him a key cog for the Orioles a few years ago. Then there's Tobias Myers , who had an up-and-down season in 2026, but could be an option as a long reliever. Elsewhere on the 40-man roster are depth options such as Jonathan Pintaro , Justin Hagenman , and Jefry Yan -- a hard-throwing lefty whom Stearns spoke highly of after the season. Minor leaguers who could possibly contribute in 2027 include hard throwers Dylan Ross and Ryan Lambert . Adrian Morejon / Imagn Images via Reuters Connect/Envato Elements/SNY Treated Image The External Options The Mets have enough intriguing bullpen depth on the roster that wholesale changes aren't needed. But it can be argued that they should be targeting a closer. That's because as dominant as Williams can be at times, he is coming off back-to-back subpar seasons. Spanning 2025 (with the Yankees) and 2026, Williams has posted a 4.65 ERA and 1.30 WHIP over 102.2 innings. In 2026, Williams' WHIP was an unsightly 1.57 as his hits per nine (9.5) and walks per nine (4.6) shot up, while his strikeout rate (11.4 per nine) dropped to its lowest level since his rookie season. That Williams' FIP over the last two seasons is 2.83 suggests he has also been unlucky. But even with that being the case, he is about to be four years removed from his last full season of dominance, which came with the Brewers in 2023. If the Mets look for a closer on the open market, the most obvious choice would be pending free agent Adrian Morejon , who will be entering his age-28 season in 2027. Over the last three years, Morejon has a 2.58 ERA (2.46 FIP) and 1.08 WHIP in 223.1 innings while striking out 248 (a rate of 10.0 per nine). A glance at Morejon's advanced stats via Baseball Savant suggests that his dominance should be sustainable. Meanwhile, his stuff -- primarily a two-seam fastball and four-seamer that both average a tick under 100 mph, and a changeup -- graded out near the top of the league. If the Padres place the qualifying offer on Morejon, however, things could get complicated. If New York turns to the free agent market for a reliever who profiles in the late innings but might not unseat Williams as the closer, Jonathan Loaisiga and Bryan Abreu stand out. The Mets should also be on the lookout for an established left-hander, with Alex Vesia being among the best options.

item.title: Newcastle United Have Found a Way to Respond After Two Consecutive Premier League Defeats
item.description: Newcastle United needed a response after two consecutive Premier League defeats, and their 2–0 victory over Crystal Palace provided an important step in the right direction. Goals from Will Osula and Harvey Barnes secured three valuable points at Selhurst Park, giving the Magpies a much-needed boost after a difficult run of results. The performance offered encouraging signs at both ends of the pitch, with Newcastle showing attacking quality while keeping a clean sheet. However, one victory does not guarantee that their problems are behind them. The challenge now is to build on this result, maintain consistency, and turn positive performances into points. With Everton approaching, Newcastle have an opportunity to prove they can start a stronger run of form this season. Newcastle United Need their attack to deliver Newcastle have many players who are capable of doing great things, but they need to find a way to get more goals in the back of the net when they are down. If Newcastle want to get up in the standings, they are going to need to find a way not to lose as they did against Coventry City. Against Crystal Palace, Will Osula and Harvey Barnes found the way to put the ball in the back of the net to secure the win 2-0. They showed that they can step up when needed to bring the win home for Newcastle fans. For Newcastle fans, scoring goals is a very important thing to do; it shows that they can still try to get into the top six in the standings. Defensive Improvement Gives Newcastle Hope A clean sheet was another good thing for Newcastle after losing two games in a row, and not letting your opponent score definitely gives you momentum for the next game. Keeping Palace from scoring shows you that they have a great defense on their roster, and that they can definitely win games. However, not every game for Newcastle will be a win, so what they need to do right now is prepare for the upcoming game against Everton. Newcastle Must Build on This Victory This victory gives Newcastle momentum, but the race is far from over. The fans want to see Newcastle bring wins home. The next game they need to focus on is Everton in the Carabao Cup; playing at home gives them the chance to bring the win home, but they never know they could be shocked and lose. If Newcastle shows what they did vs. Palace, they can definitely win; they just need to have great performances and stop many chances from scoring. Join the conversation! item.title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans fall to the New York Giants of New Jersey 27-21
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Cam Skattebo #44 of the New York Giants celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 7 Penalties…YIKES!!! 10 Penalties for 80 yards. After seeing the Giants rush for 188 yards, that is the next number that jumps out at you reading the box score. This game was in Houston, with an experienced team, facing a Giants team that hadn’t looked all that great in their last two games. Of Houston’s flags, 4 were of the mental mistake variety (3 x False Starts, 1 x Encroachment). Additionally, 3 of the penalties were offensive holding, which cost Houston 31 yards of rushing offense. The consistent lack of discipline points the finger squarely at the coaching staff. This with at least 3 flags declined, so the flag numbers could have been even worse. Bad enough when this was in Year 1 with a relatively young team. In Year 4 of the Ryans regime, with an experienced team, and at home…inexcusable, and to borrow the McClain catchphrase “pathetic”. If the Defensive Line can’t take control.. .The driving force for Houston’s defense is the defensive line. With Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr., the theory is that they should be enough to disrupt an offensive line, with the resulting impact aided the rest of the defense. However, the Giants offensive line basically negated their impact. Will Anderson Jr was a practical non-factor. While Houston sacked McCarthy 3 times, only one of those sacks came from the defensive line. Half of that total (1.5), came from defensive backs blitzing, as the final 0.5 of a sack came from a blitzing LB. If you need your defensive backfield be the catalyst of getting pressure/sacks, then this defensive scheme is not having a great day. Additionally, the Texans came into this game with a top 5 rushing defense in yards allowed/game. However, the defensive interior could not lock down the Giants’ rushing attack, especially in the 4th quarter and OT, when Houston surrendered 101 yards on the ground alone. Went from allowing less than 82 yards/game to now allowing over 98 yards/game on the ground. Home is not where the heart is: Under Ryans, the Texans entered the 2026-7 season with an 18-8 home record (2-0 in playoff games). In the previous three seasons, Houston lost no more than 3 games at home in a season. They’ve already exceeded that total this year. At best, Houston will end the season at 4-4 at home…at best. They still get all three division rivals at home, along with the Ravens, so there is potential for the home crowd to get something for their money. item.content:encoded: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Cam Skattebo #44 of the New York Giants celebrates a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 7 Penalties…YIKES!!! 10 Penalties for 80 yards. After seeing the Giants rush for 188 yards, that is the next number that jumps out at you reading the box score. This game was in Houston, with an experienced team, facing a Giants team that hadn’t looked all that great in their last two games. Of Houston’s flags, 4 were of the mental mistake variety (3 x False Starts, 1 x Encroachment). Additionally, 3 of the penalties were offensive holding, which cost Houston 31 yards of rushing offense. The consistent lack of discipline points the finger squarely at the coaching staff. This with at least 3 flags declined, so the flag numbers could have been even worse. Bad enough when this was in Year 1 with a relatively young team. In Year 4 of the Ryans regime, with an experienced team, and at home…inexcusable, and to borrow the McClain catchphrase “pathetic”. If the Defensive Line can’t take control.. .The driving force for Houston’s defense is the defensive line. With Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr., the theory is that they should be enough to disrupt an offensive line, with the resulting impact aided the rest of the defense. However, the Giants offensive line basically negated their impact. Will Anderson Jr was a practical non-factor. While Houston sacked McCarthy 3 times, only one of those sacks came from the defensive line. Half of that total (1.5), came from defensive backs blitzing, as the final 0.5 of a sack came from a blitzing LB. If you need your defensive backfield be the catalyst of getting pressure/sacks, then this defensive scheme is not having a great day. Additionally, the Texans came into this game with a top 5 rushing defense in yards allowed/game. However, the defensive interior could not lock down the Giants’ rushing attack, especially in the 4th quarter and OT, when Houston surrendered 101 yards on the ground alone. Went from allowing less than 82 yards/game to now allowing over 98 yards/game on the ground. Home is not where the heart is: Under Ryans, the Texans entered the 2026-7 season with an 18-8 home record (2-0 in playoff games). In the previous three seasons, Houston lost no more than 3 games at home in a season. They’ve already exceeded that total this year. At best, Houston will end the season at 4-4 at home…at best. They still get all three division rivals at home, along with the Ravens, so there is potential for the home crowd to get something for their money. This will be Houston’s worst home record since 2022 (0-7-1), but unlike that time, Houston should be able to win at least one home game…right? THE CRITICAL PLAY: 8:23 in OT; NYG Ball @ NYG 28; 2nd and 1; RB Cam Skattebo 42-yard run up the middle. Perhaps it was inevitable. The Texans had momentum coming into the extra frame, having just tied the game, as well as just missing out on a possible INT ball on the Giants’ final regulation drive. However, the Texans went a quick 3-and-out, punting the ball back to the Giants, who set up shop at their 19-yard line. A quick McCarthy pass got the Giants to a favorable 2nd and 1. The Giants lined up in a run formation, and McCarthy went with the handoff to Skattebo. The Giants line, aided by FB/TE Ricard, who lined up as the 2nd TE on the right side of a 3-TE set on the Giants’ right side of the line, blasted through the defensive front of the Texans. The Texans did not have a body covering the second level beyond the DL, and Skattebo had perhaps the best running lane of his pro career. From there, it was a foot race between Skattebo and the Texans’ secondary. Lassiter finally brought him down, but by then, the Giants were well within FG range. Even with their struggling kicker, it is hard to imagine that they would miss. Since Houston busted on its first OT possession, the Giants were likely going to win. Singletary’s nifty 30-yard run on the next play resolved the questions about how the Giants would clinch. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 2-0: JJ McCarthy’s record at NRG/Reliant Stadium: Combining his college and pro career, he’s played two games in Houston. This past Sunday, and when he was the starting QB for Michigan when they won the 2024 National Championship over Washington. Still has never thrown at TD in Houston, but he’ll take the combined 30 for 46 for 392 yards with no INTs and no loses. 7: Number of NFL teams since 2002 that started 2-5 and made the playoffs: If you still hold out hope, you can look to this. One of those was the 2015 Texans, who started 1-4 and 2-5, and managed to win the AFC South with a 9-7 record. They hosted another team that season (Kansas City) who also started 2-5. It did not go well . GAME BALLS: WR Xavier Hutchinson: All of the WRs on the Texans’ roster, and the most versatile one in this game ended up being Xavier Hutchinson. On the final drive, he ran for a 1st down on a jet sweep-type play, was slated to throw a WR pass and then caught the game-tying TD pass. Go figure. His final line: 3 receptions for 17 yards and 1 TD, 2 rushes for 12 yards, 3 kickoff returns for 74 yards. WR Tank Dell: Not bad when your first game action in almost 2 years after a devastating injury saw you take a pass you weren’t the primary for 43 yards to set up a tying score late in the 1st half. Also sparked the 4th quarter tying drive with his 14-yard punt return. Final line: 1 reception for 43 yards, 1 rush for 2 yards, 1 punt return for 14 yards. Giants FB/TE Patrick Ricard: He followed Harbaugh from Baltimore to East Rutherford. Good pickup. He logged no stats in the standard box score, but his blocking from the FB and the TE positions sprang the three biggest runs of the game for the Giants: the fake tush-push 3rd Down run from Skattebo for 19 yards, and the two big runs in OT combining for 72 yards and clinching the win. This game needs to lead off his future contract negotiations. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO JOHN MCCLAIN RAMBLE ON ABOUT THE BAYLOR COACHING SEARCH WHILE DROPPING HIS TRADEMARK “PATHETIC” DESCRIPTION ABOUT THE TEXANS ON REPEAT ALL WEEK. DC Matt Burke/Defensive Backs Coach Dino Vasso. Words I would not have uttered to start the year, but this pair might be sacked come Black Monday. The secondary once again was picked apart, this time by a known mercurial QB. Yes, Pitre and Blankenship were out for this game, but the communication between DBs in respective zone coverages seemed lacking, with the Giants able to rack up some explosive plays in the Texans’ defensive backfield. It is far too late in the season to be suffering comms break-downs. Throw in a defensive line that could not take advantage of a newish QB and LBs that allowed themselves to be shut down by Giants’ blockers, and you have a recipe for what you saw Sunday. Yes, Ryans is calling the plays, but whatever is going on in practice is either not translating onto the field (bad), or the performances from practice are translating to what is happening on the field (worse). OC Nick Caley/HC DeMeco Ryans :Actually, let’s put the offensive coaches as well as the overall coaching staff on this one. The offense was a bit too stubborn trying to get Marks going with the running game when turning Stroud loose might have worked out better, even given some of the pressure the Giants put on him. Ryans, well, this game had all the hallmarks of a trap game (back from big overseas win with a bye week coming), and he let the team step right into it without hesitation. Giants PK Dominic Zvada: Lost in all the hubbub about Skattebo and McCarthy was the fact that the Giants PK did

item.title: Broncos at Cardinals: The No Bull Review
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos runs for a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let this be a lesson to all of you out there in Broncos Country: don’t trust the talking heads with narratives about this team or its players. Last week all we heard about was how terrible and inept Bo Nix was. No one in the mainstream media was talking about the quality of defenses the Denver Broncos were facing or the lack of a competent run game. Most of them took their turns dumping on Bo Nix because none of them thought he was going to do anything coming out of the draft. He was mislabeled as a check-down merchant in Oregon, and that label will likely follow him every time he has a match-up against an excellent defense. Not to worry, Broncos Country. This team is who we here at the No Bull Review thought they were. This is darn near the same script we saw last season. Sit back and enjoy the ride for the rest of this season as the Broncos hit their stride. Offense Sean Payton continues to tweak the offense as he keeps the team growing and moving toward a better version of themselves as the season wears on. He gave a ton of snaps to young Jonah Coleman, signaling that he’s not satisfied with the best a back can gain on average is 3 yards. He had more plays for Mims in this game and designed a multitude of shots downfield to multiple receivers. There was still a nice balance of run (26) vs. pass (29). The big difference in this game was in explosive plays. The offense had 5 plays of 20 yards or more. There are still many things for them to clean up. Receivers had drops, linemen blew blocks, and the quarterback can place the ball better in spots for sure. I’m not saying that the offense is a group of world-beaters. I am saying this team played up to their potential and showed what they are capable of doing. Quarterbacks Bo Nix can throw downfield, in case you didn’t know. He attacked deep early and kept it up through the game. He had an absolutely masterful run for a touchdown. He threw a 27-yard pass to Waddle that was a laser. I’m going to reiterate that everyone in the media has misread the ankle injury completely. People keep mentioning it as if it is still an issue. The issue is not the ankle from a health standpoint. As we saw on his nearly 20 mph run to the promised land, the ankle is working just fine. The issue with the ankle injury comes from him getting back into his groove as a passer. His accuracy has been lacking early this season (much like it did last season). I think we’re seeing Nix rounding into form as the season wears on. He’s getting work each week finally, and as he settles his footwork down, his throws are only going to get better and better. Line I largely liked what I saw from the line this week. They only gave up one sack. The run game was blocked up wel
