They only gave up one sack. The run game was blocked up well enough. Sure, we saw McGlinchey miss a stunt and block no one to give up a big pressure. We also had a couple of illegal formation penalties that should never happen. This line has had a rough start to the season. With a more efficient runner toting the rock, I’m optimistic about their progress and ability to round into form much like Nix. Running Backs A healthy Jonah Coleman is just what the doctor ordered for this ailing Broncos run game. He was in on 50% of the snaps for the team. He showed a runner who has vision, burst, and power. I loved his ability to cut back and head north when his designed holes were closing up. That seems simple enough, but we’ve seen far too many runs go for nothing because backs aren’t cutting when the play is smothered. He averaged 6 yards per carry on 9 runs for 54 yards. He also caught two passes for 15. Coleman is versatile in anything we ask the position to do in this offense. I’m excited to see what this rookie does with the rest of his season. R.J. Harvey is a home-run hitter. He took a screen pass to the house early in the 3rd quarter. It was a perfectly timed and executed play that had multiple blockers running free downfield to help Harvey jet into the end zone. He was pretty rough as far as output goes outside of that one play. His other 4 touches were plays for 2-3 yards each. JK Dobbins had 6 carries for 23 yards. On one hand, that’s an improvement over what we’ve seen from him in the past few games. On the other hand, there’s a reason he only saw 23% of the snaps in the game. One of his carries was a touchdown that he earned fighting through a tackle to lunge the ball over the goal line. Receivers Let’s give some love to Marvin Mims for getting more involved with the offense this week. He had a gain of 47 yards off a busted coverage play to the sideline. He’s another guy on this offense who is a threat to house the ball if they can just find ways to get him the ball in space. Cortland Sutton got the party started with an in-breaking route across the middle for a big gain of 20 yards. He’s still looking like a player who has lost a step, but his size and great route running open up plays for Nix. Jaylen Waddle had a couple of really nice catches in this game. He caught a low throw on a 14-yard out that was way tougher than it needed to be. Late in the game, he caught a 27-yard back shoulder downfield while taking a big hit from a closing safety. He ended the game with 4 catches for 48 yards. Troy Franklin was ice cold in this game, missing both of his targets. What I loved from him was his blocking for the Nix run. He blocked two guys to help Nix get into the end zone. Defense The Broncos defense again held the opponents to under 20 points. That’s excellent in today’s NFL. Vance Joseph didn’t have an answer for Trey McBride (he threw everything and the kitchen sink at him coverage-wise). Sometimes you can’t hold down a great player (just ask JSN). I want to say that Joseph had his defense playing inspired football to close out the game. The Arizona Cardinals got the ball down to the 1-yard line and the defense held them out for 7 straight plays. The effort never dropped even with a two-score lead. Front 7 Malcolm Roach, to me, was the defensive player of the game. He was absolutely killing it up front all game long. He had a sack, a tackle for loss, 4 quarterback hits, and a batted pass to seal the big goal-line stand at the end of the game. Alex Singleton stacked up another really solid game. It wasn’t a shut-out for him, as he had a couple of coverage plays with shaky coverage, including a 14-yard crossing route that got by him. He had an impressive 19-tackle game with a tackle for loss, 2 quarterback hits, and a sack on the day. Sai’vion Jones had the most impressive sack of the game, with a guy draped over him using one arm. He also had a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit. Secondary Riley Moss got flagged for pass interference for executing perfect pass defense to deflect a pass as it was caught. I’m honestly sick and tired of referees throwing a flag when they see Moss in coverage. The replay made me want to puke, honestly. Riley had a pass defense later in the game with far more contact than we saw on the pass interference penalty. Kris Abrams-Draine continued to impress me with his play this week. He had an excellent open-field tackle to keep a pass bottled up on a 2nd and 5. On a 4th and 13 play out to his side, he did a superb job not biting as the receiver lateralled the ball to a guy behind him. KAD recognized what was happening and kept himself in line to stop the play. Brandon Jones on 3rd and 2 got the defense off the field with smothering coverage on McBride. He gave a huge pass interference call up by being too handsy and also had a couple of missed tackles. McMillian darn near had 3 interceptions in the game. They all go down in the stat sheet as a pass defense, but my soul weeps a bit to see so many passes hit his

item.title: Tuesday Morning Texas Rangers Update
item.description: SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 14: Jack Leiter #22 of the Texas Rangers looks on between innings of a baseball game against the Athletics at Sutter Health Park on August 14, 2026 in Sacramento, California. (Photo by Scott Marshall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning. Kennedi Landry writes about Jack Leiter hoping to bounce back from a flukish injury that started what became a lost season for the young righty. In today’s Sebastian Walcott update, FanGraphs’ Eric Longenhagen checks out the prospects at the Arizona Fall League where Walcott has looked like the cream of the crop in the desert. And, after a victory last night to go up 3-0, Thad Levine’s Brewers will have four shots at winning one more game against Jon Daniels’ Rays to join most recently the Rangers in winning the first World Series in franchise history. Have a nice day!

item.title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys win over the Eagles
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys’ losing streak is over as they came away with a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. While the final scoreboard suggests they ran away with this one, it ended up being a little more troublesome than one might’ve thought. The Eagles were short-handed, and they actually had the lead early before Dallas finally pulled away at the end. Here are 10 thoughts on this much-needed Cowboys victory. 1. Restored rushing attack The ground game finally decided to show some life and give the offense some balance. The blocking upfront was outstanding, and the holes were plentiful. The Cowboys racked up over 200 yards rushing, with 155 coming courtesy of Javonte Williams, who finished the game with over six yards per carry, including the game’s final touchdown. It was a positive step forward for a rushing attack that had been missing in action over the previous few weeks. 2. Stars a shining While Williams set the tone on the ground by running the ball, Dak Prescott did a good job of distributing the ball. He finished the game with three touchdown passes. Two of those scoring strikes found the hands of CeeDee Lamb, while the other went to George Pickens. That touchdown grab by Pickens was amazing, as he adjusted his body, hauled down the pass, and kept both feet in bounds. He’s so incredible at bringing in difficult catches that very few receivers in this league can do. 3. Welcome back, DeMo DeMarvion Overshown made his return to the lineup and provided an immediate spark for the defense. He was flying around, filling gaps, and tracking down ball carriers with authority. He filled the stat sheet, leading the team with five solo tackles, but his biggest play came when he dropped back in coverage and stepped in front of a Dallas Goedert pass and hauled in the interception. That was essentially the game-ender. 4. Impactful Q Quinnen Williams has been a disruptive force recently, and Monday night was no different. He was a complete nightmare for the opposing blockers, consistently blowing up plays before they could develop. Williams finished a dominant performance with a sack and three tackles for a loss, routinely collapsing the pocket. He almost added another highlight by making what initially looked like a fourth-down stop, but he lined up a little too close to the center and got flagged for a penalty. 5. The Goodson The team continues to roll without their All-Pro kick returner, who is recovering from a rib injury, but his absence hasn’t hurt the team. Backup running back Tyler Goodson has filled in nicely. While his return touchdown didn’t count, he showed some good explosiveness and has slowly put himself into the conversation as a useful tool for this team, on offense or even on special teams. 6. item.content:encoded: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys’ losing streak is over as they came away with a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. While the final scoreboard suggests they ran away with this one, it ended up being a little more troublesome than one might’ve thought. The Eagles were short-handed, and they actually had the lead early before Dallas finally pulled away at the end. Here are 10 thoughts on this much-needed Cowboys victory. 1. Restored rushing attack The ground game finally decided to show some life and give the offense some balance. The blocking upfront was outstanding, and the holes were plentiful. The Cowboys racked up over 200 yards rushing, with 155 coming courtesy of Javonte Williams, who finished the game with over six yards per carry, including the game’s final touchdown. It was a positive step forward for a rushing attack that had been missing in action over the previous few weeks. 2. Stars a shining While Williams set the tone on the ground by running the ball, Dak Prescott did a good job of distributing the ball. He finished the game with three touchdown passes. Two of those scoring strikes found the hands of CeeDee Lamb, while the other went to George Pickens. That touchdown grab by Pickens was amazing, as he adjusted his body, hauled down the pass, and kept both feet in bounds. He’s so incredible at bringing in difficult catches that very few receivers in this league can do. 3. Welcome back, DeMo DeMarvion Overshown made his return to the lineup and provided an immediate spark for the defense. He was flying around, filling gaps, and tracking down ball carriers with authority. He filled the stat sheet, leading the team with five solo tackles, but his biggest play came when he dropped back in coverage and stepped in front of a Dallas Goedert pass and hauled in the interception. That was essentially the game-ender. 4. Impactful Q Quinnen Williams has been a disruptive force recently, and Monday night was no different. He was a complete nightmare for the opposing blockers, consistently blowing up plays before they could develop. Williams finished a dominant performance with a sack and three tackles for a loss, routinely collapsing the pocket. He almost added another highlight by making what initially looked like a fourth-down stop, but he lined up a little too close to the center and got flagged for a penalty. 5. The Goodson The team continues to roll without their All-Pro kick returner, who is recovering from a rib injury, but his absence hasn’t hurt the team. Backup running back Tyler Goodson has filled in nicely. While his return touchdown didn’t count, he showed some good explosiveness and has slowly put himself into the conversation as a useful tool for this team, on offense or even on special teams. 6. Aubrey pinning them deep Brandon Aubrey continues to prove that his value extends beyond making field goals by weaponizing his kickoffs. He appears to have dialed in his dirty kicks, lining driving the ball to perfect locations and forcing difficult return situations. Three separate times during the second half, the Eagles’ returners failed to handle the ball cleanly, allowing the Cowboys coverage unit to swarm. Because of his precision, the opposing offense was forced to start their drives inside their own 20-yard line. 7. Third-down disaster Third downs have become so nightmarish for the Cowboys defense. Every time third down rolls around, we can hear the cryptic Michael Myers Halloween music in our heads. Something bad is about to go down. It’s frustrating, because this dysfunctional group can play somewhat well on early downs. They just can’t close the deal and get off the field. 8. Penalty problems Getting stops on defense is hard enough, but it becomes almost impossible when you are constantly fighting your own mistakes. The Cowboys’ defense spent a large part of the night shooting themselves in the foot with penalties that wiped out would-be stops. The peak of this frustration came on a fantastic kickoff return from Goodson that had fans out of their seats, only to slowly sit back down as it was nullified by a holding penalty. This stupid team, sometimes. 9. Run defense struggles While the defense eventually settled down and started making stops, it was still weird how much they struggled stopping the run, considering that’s really all the Eagles could do. Quarterback Tanner McKee wasn’t going to hurt them. Despite knowing this, they still couldn’t stop the Eagles’ rushing attack. The Cowboys caught a break that Saquon Barkley wasn’t at full health because he ran for nearly nine yards a carry, but could only muster seven rushing attempts. 10. Clock mismanagement We were graced with a little bit of excitement toward the end of the first half when it looked like the Cowboys offense was flying down the field. With just over a minute left in the second quarter and the ball on their own 13-yard line, the Cowboys marched down the field quickly. However, instead of finishing with a touchdown, they had to settle for a field goal thanks to poor clock management. Brian Schottenheimer chose not to use a timeout after a completion to Lamb with 44 seconds left, allowing precious time to come off the clock. They struck again on the very next play, getting down inside the Eagles’ 10-yard line, but they only had 12 seconds left, ultimately limiting how many shots they could take at the end zone.

item.title: Syracuse football: game time announced for home tilt against Clemson
item.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 24: Running back Ahmad Miller #22 celebrates scoring a touchdown alongside tight end David Clement #0 and tight end Noah Meyers #81 of the Syracuse Orange during the first half of their game against the North Carolina Tar Heels at Kenan Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just as Orange fans were getting used to spending their Saturday nights watching Syracuse on the ACC Network, the Orange are beginning to settle into a new trend. The kickoff time for Syracuse’s November 7 matchup against Clemson was announced yesterday, with the game set for noon inside the Dome. 🚨 Game Time Announcement 🚨 @CuseFootball vs. Clemson on Nov. 7 will be a noon kickoff at the JMA Dome. 🍊🏈🙌 🎟️ https://t.co/G3jXV2gegJ pic.twitter.com/dxuf9w1EBJ — Syracuse Athletics (@Cuse) October 26, 2026 It will mark the second consecutive home game for the Orange to kick off at noon, as well as their second straight matchup to be on ESPN2. Coming into last weekend’s game against North Carolina, the Orange had not beaten a conference opponent since defeating Clemson last season. That victory was a memorable one for Syracuse, but it also came with a setback, as quarterback Steve Angeli tore his Achilles during the third quarter of that game. Now, Syracuse will look to make it two consecutive victories over Clemson when the two teams meet on November 7. The Orange have historically struggled against the Tigers, holding a 3-10 record in the all-time series. However, it has been another down year for Clemson and their offense has had their fair share of struggles, being the only FBS team with more points from their defense/special teams than their offense. CLEMSON – stat of the year contender🚨 The only team whose D/ST is outscoring their Offense pic.twitter.com/49Yj3RFCAP — The Fourth Quarter (@4thQuarterCFB00) October 26, 2026 With the win over North Carolina, if the Orange can pull off an upset this upcoming weekend against SMU, thoughts about possibly becoming bowl eligible could be back on the table. What are your thoughts about the back-to-back afternoon starts following the three night games?

item.title: Tuesday Thoughts 10/27: Circling the Drain
item.description: Glad I didn’t watch this one live. Game Recap in Three Sentences It was a rough game on the ground as BC totaled nearly 400 rushing yards, mostly by just running the same play over and over again. Turnovers doomed an otherwise-okay-ish offensive performance from Tech. A halftime lead of one point quickly evaporated as Tech allowed BC to score on all of its real second half possessions (including touchdowns on all but one). Above The Line of the Week Grady Adamson. This was his first extended game action and he went a solid 7/9 for 73 yards and a score. Yikes that this is pretty much the only individual performance worth calling out this week. The National Air and Space Museum. Planes and rockets are sick. Cooler weather. Fourth Quarter of the Week 24 points??? Are we serious? That’s how many points a self-respecting P4 team scores against an FCS team in a quarter, not how many they should be giving up to maybe the worst team in their conference. By the way, BC only scored 22 points in their entire GAME against MAINE. Embarrassing. 5 Star (7 Star, 5 Star) Developmental Program Haiku of the Week What’s left to hope for? Eagle-eyed fans see the end Cold winds are blowing Circling the Drain After Saturday I’m left with one nagging, depressing question: what’s the path forward from here? The 2026 season is toast. We are heavy underdogs in every remaining game; according to ESPN our highest chance to win is 22% vs Clemson (lol imagine telling that to someone a few years ago). It’s entirely possible (and probably even likely) we finish at 2-10 and a cosmic certainty we finish no better than 4-8. What happens next? Justice Haynes is gone (not that it matters anyways, we might as well have stuck a walk-on behind this OL), along with probably every other major contributor. There’s certainly going to be staff turnover and severely depressed recruiting as well so we’ll be starting over for the second year in a row. Support and funding will dry up as well, and we’ll be a tough sell to any half-decent transfer prospects. Oh and guess what: the 2027 schedule is going to be much harder. It’s obviously early but I don’t really see how we can win more than 4-5 games next year. That number would suck in any season but the bigger looming problem is that I think Key needs more like 8-9 wins to save his job and still be coaching in 2028. Sure a lot could change between now and then, it is college football after all, but I’d still bet my bank account that that’s far too tall of an order. There’s simply no advantage or difference-maker or it-factor that he brings to the table to overcome the direction we’re heading in. Maybe there are valid reasons to not fire him right now but as far as I’m concerned the writing is on the wall – I don’t see a path for him to recover from this. So not only will we be starting over in 2027, we’ll probably be starting over in 2028 as well and we might see the heat death of the universe before someone actually “turns around” Georgia Tech f

I’m exhausted and cranky writing this in the airport after two straight weeks of traveling so I don’t really feel like digging into what all I think has gone wrong; we can save those few thousand words for later. Suffice it to say that I don’t think Key is the guy to turn this thing around right now. We’re just gonna be watching him slowly approach the inevitable. Back in 2022 I laid out an argument for why he shouldn’t get the job , and every single point is still applicable here in 2026 – nothing has changed. He’ll always be better than Collins, but it’s looking more and more like Haynes King deserves all the credit for that. Look Ahead Up next is Pitt (10/31, 7:30pm). Whatever man. They’ll probably comfortably win by multiple scores, just sim me to the end of the season.

item.title: 3 keys to the game: UConn men's basketball team vs. Purdue in preseason finale
item.description: UConn Huskies head coach Dan Hurley gives instruction to his team during a college basketball exhibition game between the Michigan State Spartans and UConn Huskies on October 20, 2026 at the Breslin Center in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) HARTFORD - Zach Edey isn't walking through that door (even if his 7-foot-4 frame could fit through the doorway). Trey Kaufman-Renn isn't either, though it appears he'll be in Storrs on Dec. 12 with Kansas in the midst of his sixth year of college competition. Caden Pierce will be walking through that door, not with the UConn men's basketball team but in a Purdue uniform. Perhaps most importantly for the Huskies, Braylon Mullins will not only walk through that door, he'll jump into the action for the first time this season in Tuesday's exhibition bout with Purdue (7 p.m., WFSB) at PeoplesBank Arena. Here are three keys to watch for in UConn's exhibition finale on Tuesday night: How does Braylon Mullins look in return to action? This will be the sophomore guard's first return to action since the Huskies' national championship game loss to Michigan, so he'll be on a minutes restriction. "A program like Purdue, it's a tough first game to come back for," Dan Hurley noted. "But it'll be good in terms of getting one under his belt before the real ones start." Mullins returned to practices prior to UConn's exhibition win over Michigan State last week and has looked "really sharp," per Hurley. "We know how much firepower he has at the offensive end," senior point guard Silas Demary Jr. said. "We know what a microwave scorer he can be. He can go on runs by himself, he can hit big-time shots. Having my backcourt mate back in the backcourt with me, it's great to see him out there. I don't think he's lost a step." UConn's Solo Ball and Braylon Mullins watch the team warm up before the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame Exhibition Series preseason game against Syracuse at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Conn., Tuesday, October 13, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) Is UConn ready for prime time? We all know about the Huskies' grueling non-conference schedule this season. Will exhibitions against high-caliber foes like Purdue, Michigan State, even Syracuse prepare them for the likes of Michigan, Arizona, Duke, Illinois, Ohio State, Kansas, Virginia ...? "It's going to show us where we need to grow," Demary noted. "For a young team like we are, it shows us we can play in these big-time games and big-time moments. We have a crazy non-conference schedule coming up, so I think these games will help us go through some adversity and learn where we are as a team." The Huskies have looked good in convincing wins over Syracuse and Michigan State, both without Mullins. But there's always room for improvement, particularly when it comes to their big men (Na'jai Hines and Oskar Giltay) staying out of foul trouble. Giltay fouled out of the

But there's always room for improvement, particularly when it comes to their big men (Na'jai Hines and Oskar Giltay) staying out of foul trouble. Giltay fouled out of the Syracuse game; Hines from the Michigan State contest. UConn's Silas Demary Jr. tries to speed past Syracuse's Garwey Dual during the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame Exhibition Series preseason game against Syracuse at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Conn., Tuesday, October 13, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) "The fouling has been a challenge," Hurley said. "We're not going to be successful this year if both halves of every game, both centers are in foul trouble. A lot of it is undisciplined fouling, not hedging ball-screens, fouls that are frustrating." "Start faster offensively and sustain it," Hurley summed up of his goals for Tuesday night. "Start faster defensively and sustain it for a full 40 minutes." How would Caden Pierce have looked in a UConn uniform? UConn beat Purdue in their most important battle, the 2024 national championship game. But the Boilermakers got a small measure of revenge by beating out the Huskies in a recruiting battle out of the transfer portal for Caden Pierce . The 6-foot-7 senior forward was the Ivy League Player of the Year as a sophomore at Princeton, averaging 16.6 points and 9.2 rebounds per game. Injuries limited him to 11.2 and 7.2 as a junior, and he sat out all of last season to concentrate on his academics while fielding offers out of the portal. Pierce had plenty of interest, making visits to Duke, Gonzaga, Louisville and UConn before signing with Purdue in April. It probably shouldn't have been a surprise, as Pierce has plenty of Big Ten ties. A native of suburban Chicago, his parents were athletes at Northwestern and his brother, Alec, is a wide receiver for the Indianapolis Colts. "He was a guy that we thought highly enough of to bring him in for a visit while we were in-season, and I don't like to do much recruiting in-season," Hurley noted. "So, that tells you what we thought of him. The pedigree of the family is amazing. He was an awesome fit, it's just our situation, things were so cloudy with who was going to return for us on our roster that, on his decision-making timeline, we couldn't wrap our mind around what we were going to look like at that point." In Purdue's two exhibition wins over Ball State and Purdue-Fort Wayne, Pierce has scored just seven points on 3-for-8 shooting and grabbed five rebounds in about 19 minutes of action per contest. "I don't think you can have more respect for the family or the player," Hurley continued. "And obviously, he would have fit great here, too." Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. This article originally published at 3 keys to the game: UConn men's basketball team vs. Purdue in preseason finale .

item.title: Problem or Solution: Kristian Campbell
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are stuck. If you’re the type of person who is content finishing third within the division and being bounced by your arch rivals in just a handful of games in back-to-back seasons, you might disagree. If you’re not an idiot, you know difficult decisions need to be made and that things need to change. I’ve decided to task myself with analyzing which players can be part of the turnaround and which should be shown the door, all as a way to take the heat off chief baseball officer Craig Breslow. If you’re not down with that, I’ve got two words for ya: Problem or Solution? I genuinely have no idea what the plan is… Kristian Campbell was supposed to be part of the future, but the same guy who signed an eight-year contract extension before making his big league debut just spent the entire season in the minor leagues and has been surpassed by several replacement-level players and new acquisitions on the depth chart. I’d love to blame the organization for all that, but they’ve tried him at multiple positions and have given him plenty of time to fix the issues that started to plague him at the plate after his torrid start to professional baseball. If you look at his numbers and positions played the last two seasons, you can see that there has been plenty of time and energy placed into making this whole thing work. 2025 (MLB): 67 G (59 2B, 9 OF), .223/.319/.345, 6 HR, 10 2B, 72 K, 29 BB 2025 (MiLB): 65 G (32 1B, 11 2B, 22 OF), .273/.382/.417, 8 HR, 11 2B, 84 K, 38 BB 2026 (MiLB) : 108 G ( 10 DH, 98 OF ), .256/.383/.380, 8 HR, 22 2B, 126 K, 73 BB ONCE AGAIN… I genuinely have no idea what the plan is. WHAT WE KNOW The Red Sox are stuck trying to figure out what to do with this guy — for better or worse. Campbell spent last season rebuilding his swing, which seemed to be an edict from the organization as it looked to help get him back to being the guy it dished out that contract to. I don’t necessarily know if they got him there, but improvements were made and he definitely seemed to find his footing defensively as an outfielder/designated hitter. WHAT WE DON’T KNOW I don’t know if he’s good enough to play over the likes of Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, or Curtis Mead. Boston currently plans to fill all three outfield spots and second base with those four players, while it has also made it known that designated hitter is reserved for players who need a day off from playing the field or veterans who suck doing anything else. I can’t see them making that plan work, though, which is both good and bad news for the positionless guy with a big fat contract that needs to be paid out. There’s still a ways to go, but Kristian Campbell looks like a different player than earlier in the season. Here’s an open-side look at his swing from April and then from tonight. pic.twitter.com/T2dgzRntGV — Ian Cundall (@IanCundall) August 15, 2026 BEST-CASE SCENARIO The Red Sox are able to turn him into the platoon outfielder that they’ve needed sin

item.title: Anthony Nunez flashed elite stuff in an up-and-down rookie season
item.description: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 23: Anthony Nunez #66 of the Baltimore Orioles pitches against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on August 23, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fifteen months ago, with the 2025 Orioles in the midst of a lost season, Mike Elias put a metaphorical Clearance Sale sign on the O’s roster. Everything that wasn’t nailed down was up for grabs, and in the span of a week, Elias made seven trades that jettisoned eight players from the major league squad, including Cedric Mullins, Ryan O’Hearn, and nearly half the bullpen. In return, 14 newcomers joined the Orioles’ organization. One notable fact about those 14: not a single one of them was a major league player. Even with the trades creating a litany of holes in the Orioles’ active roster, the O’s didn’t acquire anyone who would immediately fill those slots. For Birds fans anxious to get their first look at the return haul from the fire sale, they’d have to wait a while longer. Enter Anthony Nunez. The rookie right-hander, acquired from the Mets in the Mullins deal, was the first of that 2025 prospect bonanza to arrive in the bigs after earning a surprise inclusion on this year’s Opening Day roster. And by the time the season ended, he’d become one of the Orioles’ most-used arms out of the bullpen, with his 52 appearances ranking fifth on the team. Nunez’s path to the majors was circuitous, to say the least. A standout shortstop at Miami Springs HS, Nunez was drafted by the Padres in the 29th round in 2019, but was released two years later after topping out in Low-A. He took advantage of an NCAA rule that allowed former high school signees to return to college as long as it wasn’t with a Division I school, joining Division II University of Tampa in 2022. With the Spartans, Nunez became a two-way player, taking the mound for the first time in 2024 and striking out 20 batters in 11.2 innings. With his arm clearly much more intriguing than his bat, Nunez landed a minor league deal with the Mets as a full-time pitcher, where he flew through the minors and reached Double-A Binghamton in 2025. At the time the O’s acquired him for Mullins — along with fellow righties Raimon Gomez and Chandler Marsh — Nunez was laying waste to minor league hitters. He had a 0.80 WHIP, a 40% strikeout rate, and batters were hitting just .119 against him. The O’s immediately promoted him to Triple-A Norfolk, where Nunez had a bit of a ruder greeting, posting a 4.85 ERA and allowing 18 baserunners in 13 innings. He still racked up 21 strikeouts. FanGraphs in particular loved Nunez, ranking him as the Orioles’ sixth-best prospect in May, ahead of Ike Irish, Nate George, and Joseph Dzierwa, among others. Eric Longenhagen and Brendan Gawlowski pegged him as “a premium reliever with three plus or better pitches and uncommon strike-throwing consistency,” and also suggested that he could eventually be stretched out as a starter.
item.content:encoded: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 23: Anthony Nunez #66 of the Baltimore Orioles pitches against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on August 23, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fifteen months ago, with the 2025 Orioles in the midst of a lost season, Mike Elias put a metaphorical Clearance Sale sign on the O’s roster. Everything that wasn’t nailed down was up for grabs, and in the span of a week, Elias made seven trades that jettisoned eight players from the major league squad, including Cedric Mullins, Ryan O’Hearn, and nearly half the bullpen. In return, 14 newcomers joined the Orioles’ organization. One notable fact about those 14: not a single one of them was a major league player. Even with the trades creating a litany of holes in the Orioles’ active roster, the O’s didn’t acquire anyone who would immediately fill those slots. For Birds fans anxious to get their first look at the return haul from the fire sale, they’d have to wait a while longer. Enter Anthony Nunez. The rookie right-hander, acquired from the Mets in the Mullins deal, was the first of that 2025 prospect bonanza to arrive in the bigs after earning a surprise inclusion on this year’s Opening Day roster. And by the time the season ended, he’d become one of the Orioles’ most-used arms out of the bullpen, with his 52 appearances ranking fifth on the team. Nunez’s path to the majors was circuitous, to say the least. A standout shortstop at Miami Springs HS, Nunez was drafted by the Padres in the 29th round in 2019, but was released two years later after topping out in Low-A. He took advantage of an NCAA rule that allowed former high school signees to return to college as long as it wasn’t with a Division I school, joining Division II University of Tampa in 2022. With the Spartans, Nunez became a two-way player, taking the mound for the first time in 2024 and striking out 20 batters in 11.2 innings. With his arm clearly much more intriguing than his bat, Nunez landed a minor league deal with the Mets as a full-time pitcher, where he flew through the minors and reached Double-A Binghamton in 2025. At the time the O’s acquired him for Mullins — along with fellow righties Raimon Gomez and Chandler Marsh — Nunez was laying waste to minor league hitters. He had a 0.80 WHIP, a 40% strikeout rate, and batters were hitting just .119 against him. The O’s immediately promoted him to Triple-A Norfolk, where Nunez had a bit of a ruder greeting, posting a 4.85 ERA and allowing 18 baserunners in 13 innings. He still racked up 21 strikeouts. FanGraphs in particular loved Nunez, ranking him as the Orioles’ sixth-best prospect in May, ahead of Ike Irish, Nate George, and Joseph Dzierwa, among others. Eric Longenhagen and Brendan Gawlowski pegged him as “a premium reliever with three plus or better pitches and uncommon strike-throwing consistency,” and also suggested that he could eventually be stretched out as a starter. They praised Nunez’s fastball, changeup, and a slider that they called “an elite swing-and-miss pitch.” It seemed certain that Nunez would make his MLB debut this season, but it happened sooner than most expected. His impressive spring training — five scoreless innings, with no walks and six strikeouts — earned him an Opening Day roster spot, even though he’d been optioned to minor league camp weeks earlier. Nunez dazzled in his major league debut March 28, throwing two perfect innings in mop-up work against the Twins, and soon he worked his way into high-leverage roles, earning holds in three consecutive appearances in early April. After his first dozen games, Nunez was rocking a 1.35 ERA and 16 strikeouts, looking like a great find for the Birds’ bullpen. But baseball is a game of adjustments, and hitters adjusted to Nunez. Just one month later, at the end of May, Nunez’s ERA had ballooned to 5.67. He suffered six outings in which he allowed multiple runs, including a four-run blowup in Tampa Bay on May 20 when he turned a 3-1 Orioles eighth-inning lead into a discouraging 5-3 loss. In June, when closer Ryan Helsley returned from the injured list, Nunez lost his roster spot. The O’s optioned him to the minors, and he spent most of the rest of the year riding the shuttle between Norfolk and Baltimore. He spent the majority of September in the Orioles’ bullpen, and ultimately finished the season with a 4.07 ERA (and an exactly league-average 100 ERA+) in 52 games. He struck out 10 batters per nine innings, and he did a good job of keeping the ball in the park, with a 0.8 HR/9 rate. His walk rate was a bit high (3.9 BB/9) but not disastrously so. The results may not have been overly impressive, but there was a lot to like about Nunez’s repertoire. His offspeed arsenal was especially sharp. The slider that the FanGraphs duo crowed about (which is classified in Baseball Savant as a sweeper) was Nunez’s most-used pitch. He generated a 45.8 whiff percentage with it, holding batters to a paltry .147 average and .200 SLG. His changeup was also elite (.102 AVG, .163 SLG), as was a cutter that he threw only 6% of the time (.125 AVG, .313 SLG). Where Nunez struggled was with his fastball, which averaged a strong 96.1 mph but didn’t have enough movement to keep hitters off balance. Batters pounded his four-seamer for a .316 average and .561 slugging, and his sinker was simply non-competitive, surrendering a .458 AVG and .667 SLG. He’ll need to do some work on his heater this offseason so that opponents can’t just start sitting on his offspeed stuff. Nunez’s 2026 performance had its ups and downs, but he showed promise as a 25-year-old getting his first introduction to the majors. It’s not out of the question that the Orioles could try to convert him into a starter, though as yet they haven’t announced any such plans. Even if not, Nunez should have a leg up for a spot in next year’s bullpen. Not too shabby for a guy who was an infielder two years ago.

item.title: What Magnus Norman said about Jannik Sinner in 2024 after watching him practice with Stan Wawrinka
item.description: Magnus Norman enjoyed a hugely successful playing career, but his transition into coaching has seen him reach even greater heights. A sole Grand Slam final and a career-high ranking of world number two represented the best that this Swedish star had to offer before he retired, and since then he has enjoyed spells overseeing the development of Thomas Johansson, Robin Soderling, and most famously Stan Wawrinka. And now, it has been revealed that Norman is expected to join Jannik Sinner’s team for the 2027 season , with Darren Cahill planning to step down from his massively successful post and retire. This will mark a huge shake-up for the current world number one, who has been with the Australian coach for four years. Fortunately, the man he is set to hire thinks very highly of him as a player, and effectively said so when speaking in 2024. Magnus Norman’s glowing praise for Jannik Sinner back in 2024 as he becomes his coach Chatting with the Tennis Channel podcast some two years ago, Norman was discussing his preparation with Wawrinka for the upcoming event in Beijing. The Swiss superstar would suffer a first-round exit, but that was irrelevant compared to what the coach was saying about Jannik Sinner , whom they had practised with in the run-up to this event. Using the Italian as an example of all that was special about the modern-day players, Norman admitted: “You know, the pace that these top players are playing with now, it’s just incredible how they cover the court. “I’m in Beijing right now and still coaching Stan. We were hitting with Sinner yesterday, and it’s just incredible how he moves, how he covers the court. “I mean, at one point during the practice, we were looking at each other, me and Stan, and sort of a little bit laughing. It’s just that Stan was doing a great practice, you know, and he couldn’t win a point. “It’s just incredible at some point how the players are moving.” Now, Norman will get the chance to build on this exceptional movement and power. Magnus Norman’s full coaching career to date He will bring a wealth of experience into Sinner’s camp, having spent a year with Johansson, two years with Soderling, and countless years with Wawrinka. Alongside his compatriot, Norman helped guide Soderling to two Grand Slam finals, a career-high ranking of fourth in the world, and to the Paris Masters title in 2010. They parted ways as this respected coach wanted more time with his family, and whilst Soderling continued his fine form, injuries and mononucleosis sadly ended his career early. Photo by Manuela Davies/USTA via Getty Images Having enjoyed a three-year break from full-time coaching, the 50-year-old waded back in with Wawrinka. Across three different spells with the retiring legend, he helped him win all three of his Grand Slam titles, beat all of the Big Three, reach a career-high ranking of third and win the Monte Carlo Masters. As a reward for his hard work, Norman won the inaugural ATP Coach of the Year award in 2016.

item.title: The Chiefs’ defense struggled to get stops in Seattle
item.description: Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , the Kansas City Chiefs ’ defense played the bend-don’t-break style that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has sharpened throughout his time in Kansas City. Through Week 7, the Chiefs still allow the second-fewest points per game in the NFL (17.2). The defense kept the team in this game — a better kick from 45 yards by Harrison Butker would have brought the game to within a score in the fourth quarter — but regardless of the point total, the Seahawks’ offense stayed on the field. Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs and sustained five possessions for nine or more plays. The Seahawks ran 19 more plays than Kansas City and held possession for nearly 12 more minutes. The three longest drives were key turning points, and each featured third-and-longs the Seahawks converted: 1st half: 15 plays and 96 yards for a field goal 3rd & 9 and 3rd & 7 converted Second quarter: 10 plays and 66 yards for a touchdown 3rd & 6 and 3rd & 9 converted Third quarter: 13 plays and 62 yards for a field goal 3rd & 9 and 3rd & 10 converted Let’s take a closer look at why the Chiefs couldn’t get off the field when it needed to in Seattle: Man coverage lapses Early on, Spags deployed man coverage on third downs, and quarterback Sam Darnold targeted slot cornerback L’Jarius Sneed regardless of the matchup. On the opening drive, he allowed a chains-moving third-down catch out of the slot, but the Chiefs eventually forced a punt. Third-and-9 on the second drive: With wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, as the primary threat on a pass down, the Chiefs have near-safety help over the top. Here, safety Chamarri Conner brackets Smith-Njigba with cornerback Mansoor Delane in trail-man coverage, taking away a throw at the sticks. However, slot receiver Cooper Kupp — who goes in pre-snap motion to identify Sneed as his man-coverage defender — will receive the pass with a quick pass over the middle. Kupp sets Sneed up outside and beats him back across; there’s no help over the middle because linebacker Nick Bolton is in the pass rush. Darnold’s quick release was a theme of the game, especially in the first half. He averaged 2.45 seconds to throw, the third-fastest time of his career according to NFL Next Gen Stats . He completed 13 of 14 passes when throwing in 2.5 seconds or less. However, Sneed loses the inside leverage by overdoing his jam at the line of scrimmage. Gilman cheating outside opened the floodgates for the 33-yard catch-and-run over the middle, and Conner’s poor angle on the missed tackle didn’t help either. The Seahawks relentlessly attacked the Chiefs’ man coverage over the middle until Spags adjusted. Not finishing th
item.content:encoded: Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , the Kansas City Chiefs ’ defense played the bend-don’t-break style that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has sharpened throughout his time in Kansas City. Through Week 7, the Chiefs still allow the second-fewest points per game in the NFL (17.2). The defense kept the team in this game — a better kick from 45 yards by Harrison Butker would have brought the game to within a score in the fourth quarter — but regardless of the point total, the Seahawks’ offense stayed on the field. Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs and sustained five possessions for nine or more plays. The Seahawks ran 19 more plays than Kansas City and held possession for nearly 12 more minutes. The three longest drives were key turning points, and each featured third-and-longs the Seahawks converted: 1st half: 15 plays and 96 yards for a field goal 3rd & 9 and 3rd & 7 converted Second quarter: 10 plays and 66 yards for a touchdown 3rd & 6 and 3rd & 9 converted Third quarter: 13 plays and 62 yards for a field goal 3rd & 9 and 3rd & 10 converted Let’s take a closer look at why the Chiefs couldn’t get off the field when it needed to in Seattle: Man coverage lapses Early on, Spags deployed man coverage on third downs, and quarterback Sam Darnold targeted slot cornerback L’Jarius Sneed regardless of the matchup. On the opening drive, he allowed a chains-moving third-down catch out of the slot, but the Chiefs eventually forced a punt. Third-and-9 on the second drive: With wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, as the primary threat on a pass down, the Chiefs have near-safety help over the top. Here, safety Chamarri Conner brackets Smith-Njigba with cornerback Mansoor Delane in trail-man coverage, taking away a throw at the sticks. However, slot receiver Cooper Kupp — who goes in pre-snap motion to identify Sneed as his man-coverage defender — will receive the pass with a quick pass over the middle. Kupp sets Sneed up outside and beats him back across; there’s no help over the middle because linebacker Nick Bolton is in the pass rush. Darnold’s quick release was a theme of the game, especially in the first half. He averaged 2.45 seconds to throw, the third-fastest time of his career according to NFL Next Gen Stats . He completed 13 of 14 passes when throwing in 2.5 seconds or less. Third-and-7 on the same drive: In a similar man-coverage setup, it’s now Sneed who is manned up on Smith-Njigba, with safety Alohi Gilman anticipating an out-breaking throw at the sticks in help coverage. However, Sneed loses the inside leverage by overdoing his jam at the line of scrimmage. Gilman cheating outside opened the floodgates for the 33-yard catch-and-run over the middle, and Conner’s poor angle on the missed tackle didn’t help either. The Seahawks relentlessly attacked the Chiefs’ man coverage over the middle until Spags adjusted. Not finishing the play When the Chiefs turned to zone coverage, typically when closer to or in the red zone, it wasn’t as easy for Darnold to find an option to move the chains. Kansas City held Seattle to a field goal on the previously discussed possession by playing tight zone coverage on the ultimate third down. Third-and-6 from late in the first half: The Chiefs dropped seven into zone coverage with a four-man rush, and Darnold rolls to his right after not his initial reads are taken away. That sets up defensive end George Karlaftis to wrap him up for a game-changing sack, leaving Seattle on fourth down and deciding to kick a roughly 60-yard field goal. Instead, Darnold jukes Karlaftis and outruns defensive tackle Chris Jones to the sticks. It was one of the first times the Chiefs’ defensive lineman had a chance at a sack, and No. 56 in particular couldn’t come through. A few plays later, Darnold delivered a perfect pass in rhythm to Smith-Njigba, who caught the touchdown down the sideline through tight coverage by Delane on third-and-9. Third-and-9 in the third quarter: Another four-man rush with zone coverage forces Darnold out of the pocket, and without a throwing option, cornerback Nohl Williams and linebacker Nick Bolton can’t react in time to stop him from crossing the marker. A late fake by Darnold fools Bolton. Third-and-10 from the same drive: Zone and a four-man rush work once again, with a stunt by Karlaftis dissuading Darnold from a downfield throw and forcing a checkdown. Yet Bolton and Williams are again too passive in rallying to the ball, allowing the running back to gain the first down. Edge rusher R Mason Thomas’s visible frustration after the play, in which he pressured Darnold, reflects how many in Chiefs Kingdom felt. Nothing seemed to go Kansas City’s way on third-and-long in Seattle. The bottom line Despite a frustrating night, the Chiefs’ defense was close to having a winning formula. The problem is, we say the unit is “close” way too often when analyzing negative plays, whether it’s the pass rush or coverage. On the flip side, it suggests that the players on the field simply need to perform better. However, there need to be personnel wrinkles, including at slot cornerback. Sneed (14 snaps) seemed to see his playing time decrease as the night went on, and that should continue as Chris Roland-Wallace rises in that same position. We finally found a role for Jeffrey Bassa in the Chiefs' defense He played 2 snaps in Seattle, both as a QB Spy. Remember this for the Buffalo matchup pic.twitter.com/CZYX1U8TzS — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) October 27, 2026 Another wrinkle that the Chiefs teased on Sunday night was second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa playing a Quarterback-spy role. He was in on two third-down red-zone stops as part of a unique defensive formation that deployed just two pass rushers, flooding coverage with as many defenders as possible. Look out for Bassa on the field as a spy moving forward, especially against mobile quarterbacks like the Buffalo Bills ’ Josh Allen.

item.title: Deen’s Daily: Avalanche Shakeup Coming?; Postava Shines For Detroit; NHL Trade Boards
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Colorado Avalanche are back on the ice for practice. Will we see a lines shakeup? The Red Wings started their rookie goalie for the first time and he shut down Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl . Also, some new trade boards from around the league. All that and more on this edition of Deen’s Daily — October 27. Colorado Hockey Now The Avalanche are back on the ice this morning for their first practice since that abhorrent performance against the Nashville Predators on the road. I’m not sure exactly what Jared Bednar has in store — whether we’ll see new line combinations or a shakeup of any kind. But, this is one of the more intriguing practices, at least to me, in quite some time. Around The NHL Trade Boards: We have some updated trade boards around hockey circles that are worth keeping an eye on. The NHL trade deadline is still many months away, but the in-season trading could ramp up well before that. It already has in some ways with the Connor Hellebuyck deal. Here’s the latest version of Sportsnet’s trade board, courtesy of Nick Kypreos. The Athletic’s Chris Johnston also published one a little over a week ago, granted his No. 1 was Hellebuyck. Neither of them includes Avalanche players. But some of those names could be enticing for Colorado as the season drags on. Detroit Hockey Now: Michal Postava had a magnificent performance against Edmonton to help the Red Wings defeat Connor McDavid and the rest of the 8-3-1 Oilers. New Jersey Hockey Now: The Devils begin their three-game West Coast road trip in Dallas today. Will Connor Hellebuyck play? If not, then what about tomorrow at Ball Arena? Philly Hockey Now: Flyers’ veteran defenseman is going to miss more time than initially thought. Florida Hockey Now : The return of Seth Jones to Chicago was a success for the former Blackhawks defenseman. Sunday was his first game back at United Center despite being traded two seasons ago. Forever Blueshirts: The Rangers had another tough performance, this time falling to a Los Angeles Kings team that struggled to score goals for most of the season. Until now. Carolina Hockey Now: Where does Alexander Nikishin go from here after taking a low $3 million offer? It was reported by Nick Kypreos on the Real Kyper & Bourne Show that the Hurricanes and Rangers had a trade in place over the summer, pending a Nikishin extension with New York. The Rangers had offered him somewhere in the range of six years and $50 million and he turned it down. If things don’t go well this season, will Nikishin even get that much on his next deal? Related Headlines Deen’s Daily: Avs Still Getting Exposed; Heritage Classic; Nikishin Signed For How Much?! item.title: Alexia Putellas a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but the limited shortlist illustrates flaws
item.description: Neglect of African football and a third win for the Spanish great does little to challenge narrative that the prize is reserved only for top nations’ players After a four-year wait, Alexia Putellas is the queen of women’s football once again. Receiving the Ballon d’Or for a record-equalling third time to continue Spain’s domination of this award, the 32-year-old reinforces her status as one of the greatest players of all time. It was the sixth consecutive year in which the honour went to either Putellas or her international teammate, Aitana Bonmatí, and it was symbolic of Putellas’ resurgence after her comeback from the anterior cruciate ligament injury she suffered in her left knee in 2022, her refusal to surrender her career to that setback, and her majestic rise back to the top. Continue reading...

item.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
item.description: Video appears to show Mao Zedong called a ‘dictator’ Dongpeng and Mengniu end deals with the player Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘The wind goes in all directions’: Fleetwood prepare wet welcome for Arsenal at Highbury
item.description: The Premier League champions may have bigger fish to fry but can expect a feisty reception from League Two strugglers in the Carabao Cup The headlines around Fleetwood Town are rarely about what happens on the pitch. Noteworthy elements include Jamie Vardy’s celebrated status as a former player, a partnership signed with a team in Uzbekistan and the owner Andrew Pilley resigning in 2023 after being convicted of fraud, for which he was jailed for 13 years. There is often something noteworthy going on in relation to the Fylde coast club. It is no different this week, although this time football is taking centre stage as Arsenal head to Highbury Stadium on Tuesday for a Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against the League Two side. There is no link to the Gunners’ former home in Islington and the ground is a world away from what the visitors are used to, its capacity a fraction of the Emirates Stadium. The Championship side Sheffield United were deservedly beaten there in the previous round, unable to cope with their opponents or the conditions, but the Cod Army anticipate a sterner test from Mikel Arteta’s aristocrats. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net. Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno’s betrayal? ‘Toxic’ Fernandes is symptom of United’s culture of entitlement | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Michael Carrick must now deal with more dressing-room unrest after Lisandro Martínez’s attack on the board “Toxic”: this is the damning characterisation of Bruno Fernandes from one highly placed Manchester United source after the captain’s incendiary betrayal of Michael Carrick. There has surely never been a greater anti-leadership act in United’s history than Fernandes questioning the man who trusts him to unify the dressing room and execute his on-field plan. The Portuguese has proved this faith wrong at the precise moment he was required to step up and exude a defiant togetherness. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...
